title: Impact of Identity Misalignment on Review Rating and Usefulness
affiliations: Northeastern University, Northeastern Univeristy and Northeastern University - D'Amore-McKim School of Business

detail.title: Impact of Identity Misalignment on Review Rating and Usefulness
detail.abstract: This study investigates how identity misalignment between reviewers and businesses affects consumer review ratings and perceived usefulness. Drawing from social identity theory, we operationalize group-based identity misalignment as a discrepancy between the reviewer's racial identity and the racial group associated with the restaurant being reviewed. Analyzing around 4 million reviews across over 84,000 restaurants in the United States and Canada, we find that identity-misaligned (i.e., outgroup) reviewers generally give higher ratings, except when reviewing White-associated restaurants, where they give lower ratings. Reviewer experience with outgroup dining moderates these effects. Furthermore, reviews written by outgroup reviewers are generally perceived as less useful, but this pattern reverses for White-associated restaurants, where such reviewers are perceived as more useful. By introducing identity misalignment as a novel lens for understanding consumer review behavior, this study contributes to identity-based theories of consumption and offers actionable insights for restaurants and review platforms.

title: Consumer preference-driven behavioral modeling: A joint contrastive learning recommendation model for learning specific and shared preferences
affiliations: Hefei University of Technology, Hefei University of Technology, Hefei University of Technology and Hefei University of Technology

detail.title: Consumer preference-driven behavioral modeling: A joint contrastive learning recommendation model for learning specific and shared preferences
detail.abstract: Multi-behavior recommendation aims to infer consumer preference from various auxiliary behaviors and predict target behavior. However, capturing consumers’ intrinsic preferences based on their behavioral footprints is challenging, as behaviors during the shopping process are influenced by diverse preference factors. These factors can be broadly categorized into two types: specific preferences that reflect personalized tendencies, and shared preferences that capture consistency. Driven by the interaction between two preferences, consumer behavior patterns often exhibit variability and interdependence. If the core preferences that drive behavioral changes are not accurately identified during learning, both model training and recommendation outcomes may suffer from bias. In this paper, we explore the transitions and complementarity of preferences within the marketing funnel and propose a novel Preference-driven Multi-behavior joint contrastive learning framework (P-MDCL), which consists of two preference extraction tasks and a unified contrastive learning scheme. First, we model behavior-specific preferences using consumer sub-behavior sequences and design a target–auxiliary behavior contrastive learning strategy to capture consumer preferences under the target behavior. In addition, we construct a consumer preference graph based on historical consumer–item interactions, which propagates and aggregates the implicit information embedded in consumer behaviors to integrate multi-behavior features into shared preferences. Finally, we perform joint contrastive learning to fuse the representations learned from both specific and shared preferences, thereby enhancing consumer and item embeddings through collaborative signals. Experiments on three real-world datasets show that P-MDCL outperforms state-of-the-art models.

detail.title: Mobile Internet Connectivity and Household Wealth in the Philippines

publicationDetails.detailsText: ADB Economics Working Paper Series No. 818
publicationDetails.journalName: ADB Economics Working Paper Series

detail.abstract: Mobile internet has become a fundamental component of modern infrastructure. In this paper, we consider the impact of mobile internet connectivity on household wealth in the Philippines. We construct a granular measure of local mobile internet connectivity using comprehensive information on approximately 0.27 million geocoded cell towers, and identify causal impact through a novel instrumental variable based on proximity to submarine cable landing points. Our results suggest that mobile internet connectivity significantly increases household wealth, with effects that persist across education levels and are more pronounced in urban areas compared to rural ones. Combining individual survey datasets with Points-of-Interest data, we investigate mechanisms and demonstrate that improved connectivity stimulates activities in several key economic sectors that create employment opportunities. Additionally, mobile internet connectivity enhances individual educational outcomes and promotes female labor force participation, though predominantly in occasional or seasonal roles.

title: The Definitive HealthTech Investment Intelligence Compendium 2025

detail.title: The Definitive HealthTech Investment Intelligence Compendium 2025
detail.abstract: The global healthtech investment ecosystem reached an unprecedented inflection point in 2025, with $9.9 billion deployed across 351 meticulously selected transactions through Q3 2025, marking a fundamental restructuring of healthcare delivery, operational efficiency, and patient care optimization. This transformation is driven by artificial intelligence integration at scale, value-based care proliferation, regulatory maturation, and geographic market expansion, collectively creating the largest investment opportunity in healthcare history. AI-enabled healthtech startups dominated digital health funding with a 69% share in Q2 2025, forecasting an AI healthcare market growth from $39.25 billion in 2025 to $188 billion by 2030. Market dynamics reveal mega-round capital concentration reshaping investment patterns, significant growth in emerging markets (notably India), and a robust exit landscape generating $16.4 billion across 113 transactions in H1 2025. The report presents comprehensive strategic frameworks for venture capital excellence, encompassing market dynamics, technology transformation, geographic diversification, investment funnel optimization, risk assessment, and exit strategies, guiding institutional investors through sophisticated portfolio construction and strategic positioning for the evolving healthtech ecosystem into 2026 and beyond.

title: The Evolution of Insurance Purchasing Behavior: An Empirical Study on the Adoption of Online Channels in Poland
affiliations: Jagiellonian University, ,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, National Louis University - Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, MAMASTUDIO Pawlik, GLOBAL HYDROGEN spółka akcyjna and WSB Merito University

detail.title: The Evolution of Insurance Purchasing Behavior: An Empirical Study on the Adoption of Online Channels in Poland
detail.abstract:
Purpose: The aim of this study is to examine the evolution of insurance purchasing behavior in Poland, with a focus on the growing role of online distribution channels. The paper seeks to understand the motivations, preferences, and concerns influencing consumer choice between digital and traditional methods.
Design/methodology/approach: The research uses a quantitative approach based on a structured online survey of 100 respondents. It explores demographics, purchasing habits, channel preferences, and decision-making factors such as price, trust, and convenience. The analysis identifies behavioral patterns related to digital adoption.
Findings: The results show a clear increase in the use and acceptance of online channels, especially for simple insurance products. Consumers appreciate the speed, availability, and price comparison offered by digital tools. However, some still prefer traditional channels for complex purchases due to trust and clarity. A hybrid approach is emerging, combining digital access with agent support.
Research limitations/implications: The study is limited by its sample size and focus on the Polish market. It does not explore differences by insurance product type. Future research could expand the sample and analyze specific product categories or the role of AI tools in shaping digital insurance experiences.
Practical implications: The findings suggest that insurers should improve the usability, transparency, and security of digital platforms. At the same time, maintaining advisory services is essential to support customers who seek personal guidance. Omnichannel strategies appear to be the most effective.
Social implications: Digital channels enhance access to insurance, especially for tech-savvy or remote users. Addressing concerns about trust and data privacy may increase consumer confidence and promote digital inclusion in the financial sector.
Originality/value: This paper provides empirical data on Polish consumers' online insurance purchasing behavior. It offers valuable insights into digital trends in the insurance sector and supports strategic decision-making in marketing and service design.

title: Workers’ Exposure to AI Across Development Stages
affiliations: Institute for Structural Research (IBS), Institute for Structural Research (IBS) and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Economics

detail.title: Workers’ Exposure to AI Across Development Stages

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper develops a task-adjusted, country-specific measure of workers exposure to Artificial Intelligence (AI) across 108 countries. Building on Felten et al. (2021), we adapt the Artificial Intelligence Occupational Exposure (AIOE) index to worker-level PIAAC data and extend it globally using comparable surveys and regression-based predictions, covering about 89% of global employment. Accounting for country-specific task structures reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity: workers in low-income countries exhibit AI exposure levels roughly 0.8 U.S. standard deviations below those in high-income countries, largely due to differences in within-occupation task content. Regression decompositions attribute most cross-country variation to ICT intensity and human capital. High-income countries employ the majority of workers in highly AI-exposed occupations, while low-income countries concentrate in less exposed ones. Using two PIAAC cycles, we document rising AI exposure in high-income countries, driven by shifts in within-occupation tasks rather than employment structure.

title: Cohabitation, Child Development, and College Costs
affiliations: University of Mannheim and IZA, University of Bonn, Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland and University of Leicester

detail.title: Cohabitation, Child Development, and College Costs

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: US college-educated couples with children marry at higher rates than those without a college degree. We argue that marriage, which entails lower separation risk and more equitable asset division if separation occurs, provides insurance to the lower-earning spouse, facilitating child investment. Investing in children is more valuable for college-educated couples, who are more likely to send their children to college. Using an OLG model of marriage, cohabitation, wealth accumulation, and educational investments where college is costly and completion is risky, we find that high college costs reduce incentives to marry among couples without a college degree. These differences in union choice by education heighten differences in childrens educational attainment and reduce intergenerational mobility.

title: Unpacking the Countercyclicality of Post-Secondary Enrollment in the United States
affiliations: Charles University in Prague - CERGE-EI, a joint workplace of Charles University and the Economics Institute of the Czech Academy of Sciences, York University, University of Saskatchewan, University of Amsterdam and William & Mary

detail.title: Unpacking the Countercyclicality of Post-Secondary Enrollment in the United States

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Using data from the Current Population Surveys Education Supplement for 1977-2023, we explore two important, yet understudied facets of the pattern of countercyclical post-secondary education (PSE) enrollment in the U.S. First, we show that economic downturns are associated with higher enrollment probabilities at both 2- and 4-year colleges among young men, but only at 2-year institutions among young women. Second, we show that the overall increase in enrollment propensities during downturns is primarily driven by persistence (i.e., changes in enrollment among individuals with prior PSE participation), rather than matriculation (i.e., new enrollments). However, higher unemployment rates increase matriculation probabilities at 2-year colleges among 18-year-old men and women, and at 4-year colleges among individuals in their early 20s. Our findings improve our understanding of the dimensions along which aggregate economic fluctuations induce changes in human capital acquisition.

title: The Lasting Effects of Working While in School: A Long-Term Follow-Up
affiliations: Tilburg University, Universidad de la Republica, Bocconi university and World Bank

detail.title: The Lasting Effects of Working While in School: A Long-Term Follow-Up

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper provides the first experimental evidence on the long-term effects of work-study programs, leveraging a randomized lottery design from a national program in Uruguay. Participation leads to a persistent 11 percent increase in formal labor earnings seven years after the program, driven by a 4 percent increase in the monthly probability of being employed and a 6 percent increase in monthly wages. Effects are significantly larger for men, while remaining positive for women. The program is highly cost-effective, outperforming most job training programs and reaching levels comparable to early childhood investments.

title: Virtual Reality - A Novel Method for the Future of Marketing
affiliations: Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Department of Marketing Management and Erasmus University Rotterdam (EUR) - Rotterdam School of Management (RSM)

detail.title: Virtual Reality - A Novel Method for the Future of Marketing
detail.abstract: Virtual reality (VR) technologies are advancing rapidly and are already used in business practice, yet their adoption in academic marketing research remains limited. This paper evaluates the potential of VR as a research method and provides actionable guidance for its use. We identify three distinctive features of VR studies that create value for marketing research: (1) participant immersion in realistic environments, (2) flexible manipulations of marketing contexts, and (3) automated tracking of behavioral and process data. Based on these features, we develop a framework to help researchers assess when VR is likely to add value relative to other methods. We illustrate feasibility of VR studies based on a practitioner survey and workshop, and a lab based VR study, yielding ten key insights and implications for academic research. Finally, we outline ten opportunities where VR can advance marketing knowledge and provide guidelines for designing and implementing VR studies. Together, these contributions position VR as a transformative tool for addressing substantive research questions that extends the methodological toolkit available to marketing scholars.

title: The Psychological Evolution of Children as a Driver of Economic Development: A Comprehensive Interdisciplinary Analysis
affiliations: and Presidency University

detail.title: The Psychological Evolution of Children as a Driver of Economic Development: A Comprehensive Interdisciplinary Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no known competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper. This research was conducted independently, without external funding, institutional sponsorship, or conflicts of interest. The views expressed are solely those of the author.

detail.abstract: This study proposes a novel interdisciplinary framework positioning the psychological evolution of children as a central driver of long-term economic development. Drawing on developmental psychology, neuroscience, and growth theory, it argues that shifts in children's cognitive, emotional, and moral capacities-cultivated through education, family environments, and social institutionsshape national innovation, productivity, and institutional quality across generations. Using crossnational panel data from the OECD, World Bank, UNICEF, and World Values Survey, the research constructs a composite Psychological Capital Index (PCI) encompassing creativity, resilience, emotional intelligence, and interpersonal trust among youth. Econometric analyses reveal that higher PCI values significantly predict subsequent increases in GDP per capita, innovation intensity, and institutional effectiveness, even after controlling for traditional determinants such as education, inequality, and governance. The findings suggest that investing in children's socio-emotional and cognitive development yields compounding economic returns, reframing early childhood and educational policy as foundational economic strategies. The paper concludes by advocating a paradigm shift toward a human-centered model of development that recognizes psychological capital as a form of productive wealth transmitted across generations.

title: The Visual Moderation Effect: How the Representation of Loyalty Reward Progress Affects Consumer Judgments and Behaviors
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Indiana University - Kelley School of Business - Department of Marketing, Seattle University and University of Georgia

detail.title: The Visual Moderation Effect: How the Representation of Loyalty Reward Progress Affects Consumer Judgments and Behaviors

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science (2025), forthcoming

detail.abstract: Across nine studies (N = 3,735) and a single-paper meta-analysis, the authors find evidence of a visual moderation effect, defined as the tendency for consumers to make progress estimates that are closer to the midpoint of a range (i.e., less extreme) when presented with loyalty reward progress information in a more visual format. Results indicate that when actual reward progress is displayed more visually, loyalty program (LP) members overestimate their progress when they are far from their reward but underestimate it when they are near their reward. The authors further demonstrate that this effect arises because the inherent ambiguity of more visual (vs. more numerical) representations leads consumers to feel less confident about the progress they have achieved and, consequently, to assume that they are closer to the middle of the feasible range. This visual moderation effect, which influences consumers' motivation and their propensity to undertake behaviors that would help them achieve their loyalty reward (e.g., patronizing the firm again), is robust across 1) different visual formats (i.e., progress presented in a block bar chart, a circular ring format, or with progress markers), 2) various LP contexts/categories (i.e., coffee shop, grocery store, frozen yogurt shop, car wash, restaurant), and 3) different samples (online panel participants, university students, actual customers).

title: Analysis of Managerial Behaviors in Business Management
affiliations: , National Louis University - Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Jagiellonian University,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Polsko Japońska Akademia Technik Komputerowych, Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, MAMASTUDIO Pawlik,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Pomorska Szkoła Wyższa w Starogardzie Gdańskim and WSB Merito University

detail.title: Analysis of Managerial Behaviors in Business Management
detail.abstract:
Purpose: The primary aim of this research is to empirically investigate the situational adaptability of managerial behaviors and their impact on organizational effectiveness through the practical application of Kenneth Blanchard's diagnostic tool. Design/methodology/approach: The objectives are achieved by employing a scenario-based diagnostic questionnaire derived from Kenneth Blanchard's situational leadership model to analyze managerial behaviors and their adaptability in ten selected companies. Findings: The research revealed that the supportive (affiliative) management style dominated among managers, significantly influencing team cohesion and morale, although its effectiveness depended heavily on clear goal-setting and effective feedback mechanisms. Research limitations/implications: The research underscores the need for managerial training to emphasize situational adaptability and the strategic combination of supportive and delegating leadership styles to enhance organizational effectiveness and economic performance. Practical implications: The research provides practical guidelines for enhancing leadership development programs by promoting flexible use of management styles, which can improve employee engagement, decision-making efficiency, and ultimately drive better business performance and competitiveness.

Social implications: The research may positively impact society by promoting emotionally intelligent and adaptable leadership, fostering healthier workplace relationships, reducing conflict, and contributing to improved employee well-being and organizational culture. Originality/value: The novelty of the paper lies in its practical application of Blanchard's situational leadership model to real business environments, offering empirical insights into managerial style correlations and adaptability, making it valuable for researchers, HR professionals, and organizational leaders aiming to improve leadership effectiveness.

title: The Integrated Strategic Framework of Set Menu Sales: A Practical Theory for Merging Customer Experience, Operational Efficiency, and Profitability
affiliations: Foods Support MORICA Co., Ltd.

detail.title: The Integrated Strategic Framework of Set Menu Sales: A Practical Theory for Merging Customer Experience, Operational Efficiency, and Profitability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The study involved staff interviews, field observations, and analysis of anonymized operational data. Informed consent was obtained from all participants, and no personally identifiable information was collected.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This paper redefines set menu (bundled) sales in the restaurant industry as an integrated strategic framework rather than a short-term sales tactic. Bridging Service Dominant Logic (S-D Logic), Lean Management, and the Theory of Constraints (TOC), we theorize and test a mid-range model that links five strategic objectivescustomer satisfaction, operational efficiency, profitability, value signaling, and customer loyalty-to concrete operational mechanisms. Extending recent S-D Logic developments, we incorporate resource integration and institutions/institutional arrangements within a service ecosystem perspective to explain how customers and firms jointly co-create value by simplifying decision making and stabilizing service delivery through set menu design. Methodologically, we adopt a single-case, mixed-methods design (Baby Face Planetʼs Agui branch, Aichi, Japan). Quantitative indicators (POS records, sales per labor hour-SPLH, average check, table turnover, labor cost ratio) are triangulated with qualitative evidence (manager/staff interviews, SOPs, field observations). Findings show that set menus (i) reduce customersʼ cognitive load and increase perceived fairness, (ii) lower process variability via SOP standardization, and (iii) focus throughput at peak times, raising SPLH to \5,963. The study contributes a mid-range theoretical integration and reframes set menus as a management device for training, SOP discipline, and peak load control.

title: Multi-Task Learning for Customer Base Analysis: Evidence from 966 Companies
affiliations: , University of Maryland - Robert H. Smith School of Business and Boston University - Questrom School of Business

detail.title: Multi-Task Learning for Customer Base Analysis: Evidence from 966 Companies
detail.abstract: Companies across different industries increasingly rely on customer-related measures as leading indicators of future cash flow and valuation. However, existing approaches in customer base analysis face practical limitations: parametric models often fail to capture irregular real-world dynamics; customer-firm valuation methods depend solely on aggregate metrics even when granular data are available; and independently modeling of customer behaviors overlooks their interdependencies. This paper develops the customer-based multi-task transformer (CBMT), a prediction framework that addresses these gaps through a flexible multi-task learning architecture. The approach leverages shared representations across behavioral processes while maintaining task-specific specialization, enabling joint prediction of upstream behaviors (acquisition, repeat purchases, order values) and downstream outcomes (cohort revenue, total sales). It incorporates downstream revenue objectives as auxiliary tasks to ensure behavioral predictions translate coherently into financial projections. Validation on 966 companies across 25 industries over 37 months shows 35-66% improvement in revenue prediction accuracy over benchmark models, with CBMT performing best for 60–70% of firms. The CBMT outperforms Wall Street consensus estimates by 28-34%. We provide insight into the drivers of this outperformance and conditions under which the model performs better or worse via ablation and performance heterogeneity analyses.

title: Progressive Urban Electoral Politics: Coalition Building and Electoral Breakthrough in the 2025 New York City Mayoral Race
affiliations: Lebanese University

detail.title: Progressive Urban Electoral Politics: Coalition Building and Electoral Breakthrough in the 2025 New York City Mayoral Race
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study examines how Democratic Socialist candidate Zohran Mamdani overcame structural constraints to win the 2025 New York City mayoral primary, addressing theoretical gaps between structural limitations facing progressive politics and empirical evidence of electoral breakthroughs in major American cities. Design/methodology/approach: Using a mixed-methods case study design, this research integrates quantitative electoral analysis with qualitative examination of campaign strategies (see Table I). Data sources include NYC Board of Elections results, systematic media coverage analysis, campaign materials, and demographic breakdowns. The theoretical framework combines urban regime theory, intersectionality theory, and social movement theory to analyze coalition dynamics and institutional transformation. Findings: Mamdani's victory demonstrates how progressive candidates can build winning coalitions through "transformative incrementalism"-pursuing immediate material improvements while constructing organizational capacity for systemic change. His comprehensive platform ($30 minimum wage, fare-free transit, city-owned grocery stores, rent stabilization) succeeded despite controversial international solidarity positions, revealing new possibilities for integrating antiimperial consciousness with local organizing. Research limitations/implications: Single-case analysis limits generalizability; longitudinal research tracking implementation challenges would strengthen findings. Originality/value: This study provides the first comprehensive academic analysis of a Democratic Socialist mayoral victory in America's largest city, introducing the concept of "transformative incrementalism" and demonstrating how progressive electoral campaigns can navigate structural constraints while building transformative coalitions.

title: The Role of Communication in Effective Business Management
affiliations: National Louis University - Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu, ,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Jagiellonian University,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, Polsko Japońska Akademia Technik Komputerowych, Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, MAMASTUDIO Pawlik, Pomorska Szkoła Wyższa w Starogardzie Gdańskim and WSB Merito University

detail.title: The Role of Communication in Effective Business Management
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to investigate the role of communication in effective business management by comparing internal communication systems in two companies, focusing on managerial practices, employee perceptions, and communication tools. Design/methodology/approach: A quantitative survey of 220 employees assessing 15 aspects of internal communication. Statistical methods identified key differences and patterns. Findings: Company X outperforms Company Y in all communication areas, showing higher clarity, better feedback culture, and stronger use of technology. Research limitations/implications: The study is limited to two companies in one sector and country. Results are based on self-reported data. Practical implications: Investing in feedback systems, digital tools, and participatory models improve communication effectiveness. Social implications: Strong internal communication supports trust, inclusion, and job satisfaction. Originality/value: The study offers rare, data-driven comparison of communication practices in similar companies within one industry.

title: A Manifesto for Business Schools: A Conceptual Framework for AI Relevance
affiliations: Narxoz University

detail.title: A Manifesto for Business Schools: A Conceptual Framework for AI Relevance
detail.abstract: Business schools are awash with AI pilots and tool talk, yet thin on outcomes, measurement, and operating models that change how people learn and work. This paper offers a practical blueprint. It integrates four pillars into a single framework. The AI Matrix sets the target by pairing Access with Agency to define movement toward Full Empowerment rather than passive use. The AI Passport replaces one-off credentials with a portable, renewable stack that verifies AI literacy, human-AI collaboration, evaluation, and ethical innovation across AI-Replaced, AI-Augmented, and AI-Created roles. A creativity-first curriculum addresses the documented creativity gap and treats creative judgment as a core, assessable outcome. Orchestrated Intelligence provides the workflow architecture for hybrid human-AI work, specifying task decomposition, iterative checkpoints, parameter control, tone calibration, and auditability. We synthesize recent sector evidence and align it with prior authored frameworks to move the discussion from tools to capability, governance, and proof. The contribution is a clear outcomes lens, a credential architecture that travels, and an operating model that any committed school can implement and measure. The paper is conceptual and illustrative. It proposes metrics and design moves that can be tested in future empirical studies.

title: Relationship between Nurses' Job Satisfaction and their Performance in a Government Hospital in the Philippines
affiliations: World Citi Colleges, Social Security System, Rizal Technological University, Veterans Memorial Medical Center, National Children’s Hospital, Dr. Jose Fabella Memorial Hospital and WORLD CITI COLLEGES

detail.title: Relationship between Nurses' Job Satisfaction and their Performance in a Government Hospital in the Philippines
detail.abstract: Nurses' job satisfaction is generally considered to be directly related to their performance, implying that job satisfaction enhances a nurse's performance. This study assessed the relationship between nurses’ job satisfaction and their performance in a government hospital in the Philippines. It utilized a descriptive-quantitative research method employing the adapted questionnaire with 176 nurses as a target respondent. The data were collected from the respondents using a google questionnaire thru a quick-response code and a printed questionnaire were provided for nurses assigned in areas with limited internet connection, data was analyzed using the frequency, percentage, weighted mean and the Pearson Correlation coefficient as statistical tools.   Findings revealed strong evidence that respondents generally have a positive perception of their work satisfaction. Additionally, the respondents acknowledged that various workplace factors significantly influence their job performance. The Pearson correlation analysis further indicated a positive relationship between nurses’ job satisfaction and their performance. Based on these findings, the study provides valuable insights for the subject government hospital to implement initiatives enhancing both job satisfaction and performance of their nurses.  This study can serve as a reference in devising healthcare policies and programs, emphasizing the need for systemic improvements to support nursing productivity and enhance patient care in a hospital setting.

title: The Grey-Black Spectrum: Institutional Erosion and Narrative Capture in Urban Governance
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU)

detail.title: The Grey-Black Spectrum: Institutional Erosion and Narrative Capture in Urban Governance
detail.abstract: This paper takes Hangzhou as a case study to systematically analyze the lineage structure and evolutionary logic of the grey-black industry in modern society. The article first proposes the "Interception-Obfuscation-Protection" constant tri-chain as the genetic code of the grey-black industry; then it sorts out its evolutionary tree of industry clustering, from bottom-level labor and violence drivers, to mid-level chains and cash loopholes, and finally to top-level narratives and institutional interfaces; and through the Hangzhou case, it demonstrates the panoramic evolution of the grey-black industry from construction, prepaid models to informatization and consultancy veneer. This paper points out that the uniqueness of Hangzhou lies in its highly modernized and white-collar grey-black model, which completes institutional parasitism by leveraging platform logic and policy narratives, thereby marginalizing institutional constraints within the "GDP first" development logic. Through regional and global comparisons, this paper further compares the Hangzhou model with the gang-like models of second and third-tier cities, as well as typical international grey-black forms characterized by financialization, violence, resource exploitation, and symbolization, emphasizing that the unique risk of Hangzhou lies in institutional erosion and narrative hijacking. Finally, the article proposes a governance philosophy of "Release-Rein-in-Stabilize (Fang-Shou-Wen)": activating innovation through limited pilots and clear red lines, correcting risks through institutional solidification and campaign-based adjustments, and maintaining long-term steady state through internal immunity mechanism and external "Sword of Damocles". The conclusion holds that underdeveloped cities, if they are to avoid becoming a "second Hangzhou," must regard institutional credit (credibility capital) as a core asset, and under the dual mechanisms of external pressure and internal repair, form a dynamic steady state of grey-white circulation, in order to achieve a win-win situation of development and stability.

title: The Transformative Impact of Blockchain Technology on Accounting and Auditing

detail.title: The Transformative Impact of Blockchain Technology on Accounting and Auditing
detail.abstract: Blockchain has evolved from a specialized infrastructure for cryptocurrencies to a general infrastructure for reliable data sharing. Accounting and auditing depend on documented facts, strong internal controls, and independent verification. However, the fundamental principles of blockchain-decentralization, immutability, and programmable logic-may transform those industries by automating core functions. We propose a novel framework to evaluate the impact of blockchain based on findings from a mixed method study that leverages peer-reviewed published literature and industry-based insights. Our work examines whether and how distributed ledgers improve product and organization data integrity, increase audit effectiveness and efficiency, redefine the professional role, and impact regulatory scrutiny. We suggest that blockchain has the potential to dramatically reduce the cost of reconciliation, allow for near real-time reporting, and facilitate continuous assurance-if governance, privacy and standardization can keep pace. The paper presents testable propositions, relates the full range of blockchain capabilities to auditing standards and outlines a practical, evidence-based adoption funnel that can help firms assess potential use cases. The paper's conclusion presents implications for educators and regulators and suggests possibly diversified avenues for future empirical investigation.

title: Systematic Serendipity: The 3CO Framework for Recognizing and Harnessing Strategic Possibilities in Uncertain Environments
affiliations: Independent researcher

detail.title: Systematic Serendipity: The 3CO Framework for Recognizing and Harnessing Strategic Possibilities in Uncertain Environments
detail.abstract: While strategic management acknowledges that chance, luck, and serendipity significantly influence organizational outcomes, these phenomena remain largely treated as exogenous variables beyond managerial control. This paper introduces the 3CO Framework (Context, Conditions, Constraints, and Outcomes) to demonstrate that serendipity can be systematically engineered rather than passively awaited. Drawing from Bayesian probability theory, we distinguish between specific outcomes (which remain unpredictable) and probability of discovery (which can be systematically influenced). We develop five propositions showing how organizations create high-probability discovery states through systematic context scanning, absorptive capacity development, and constraint engagement. Empirical illustration 1 This paper has been submitted for review to the Strategic Management Journal special issue on Chance, Luck, and Serendipity in Strategy and Management. through contemporary and historical cases demonstrates how apparent "luck" reflects structured capability. The framework operationalizes serendipity for quantitative research while providing actionable guidance for practitioners seeking to convert strategic helplessness into agency.

title: Employing Data Imputation to Track Poverty and Welfare Trends over Extended Time Periods: An Application to a Poorer Country
affiliations: World Bank - Development Data Group (DECDG) and Vietnam National University (VNU)

detail.title: Employing Data Imputation to Track Poverty and Welfare Trends over Extended Time Periods: An Application to a Poorer Country

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Obtaining comparable poverty estimates over time is critical for monitoring poverty trends and informing effective poverty reduction policies. Yet hardly any developing countries could construct consistent poverty trends over extended time periods due to changes to the consumption survey questionnaires and poverty lines that reflect changing consumption patterns and living standards. Furthermore, spatial and temporal deflators could be unavailable or could have been unsystematically employed, which could result in worsening incomparability of consumption aggregates. We propose a solution to these data challenges by applying data imputation to 13 survey rounds for Viet Nam during 1993-2022. Our results provide new, comparable, and smoother estimates of poverty trends for Viet Nam. We also offer a useful case study for other similar contexts.

title: A Study on the Impact of Cultural Prejudice on Social Dynamism in a Multicultural Classroom
affiliations: and St.Xavier's College,(Autonomous)

detail.title: A Study on the Impact of Cultural Prejudice on Social Dynamism in a Multicultural Classroom
detail.abstract: This research aims to investigate the extensive nature of cultural prejudice among students at the higher secondary level by synthesizing their varied experiences and it's influence on the social dynamics in a classroom premise. In most Indian educational institutions, the managerial boards, stakeholders and institutional personnel emphasize on the deep insight and significance of socially sensitized curricula, educational experiences and strategies that aid a multicultural and unified classroom structure. However, intergroup relations, biases, and the dominance of certain cultural ideologies often disrupt this ideal, leading to disparities in classroom harmony. Multicultural classrooms frequently become arenas for diverse social interactivity and exchange among learners. The study focuses on examining various forms of cultural prejudice that are still prevalent within the classroom premises, enquire into the inter group and intra group social dynamics amongst peers and investigate the extrinsic causal factors affecting and hindering social integration of all students in a multicultural classroom. This research is supported by a questionnaire administered on 105 Class XI and XII students from educational institutions in Kolkata. Findings reveal the continual prevalence of cultural prejudice, emphasizing its adverse effects on the inter and intra group social structuring, additionally highlighting the influence of diverse causal factors present in the proximate educational milieu.

title: System Modelling of Hybrid Warfare in Grey Zones: An Analysis of Synergistic Effects between Disruptive Networks and Financial Market Manipulation
affiliations: Dhurakij Pundit University

detail.title: System Modelling of Hybrid Warfare in Grey Zones: An Analysis of Synergistic Effects between Disruptive Networks and Financial Market Manipulation
detail.abstract: This study examines an emerging yet systematically uncharacterised strategic attack pattern: adversaries, without declaring war, simultaneously orchestrate infrastructure disruption incidents within target nations using highly dispersed, deniable small-scale infiltration units. Concurrently, they pre-establish short-selling financial positions in global capital markets, leveraging panic narratives to precipitate rapid downgrades in sovereign credit ratings and key corporate valuations. This enables arbitrage opportunities and self-financing for subsequent operations. This paper defines this as an evolved form of 'grey zone hybrid warfare,' noting its lethality has shifted from physical destruction to 'credit damage': the target nation remains legally at peace yet is rapidly priced as a high-risk entity in capital markets, facing increased financing costs, forced fiscal bailouts, and undermined governing legitimacy. To explain this mechanism, this paper proposes a 'dual-layer synergistic model': the upper layer comprises a discrete disruption network (multiple, small-scale, low-attributability physical disruptions), while the lower layer is the financial exploitation layer (converting these events into realisable profits via put options, sovereign credit default swaps, and similar instruments). The two layers are coupled through a 'disruption-pricing feedback loop': pre-emptive betting → multi-point disruptions → amplified narratives of 'state failure' → markets treating local incidents as systemic risks → downgraded sovereign credit and corporate valuations → profit recovery and reinvestment, forming an expandable attack industrial chain. This paper proposes three quantitative metrics: the market overreaction coefficient β (measuring the extent to which single incidents are perceived as systemic collapse evidence), the self-financing ratio SFR (arbitrage gains/action costs, where SFR>1 indicates attacks can self-sustain and scale), and credit-grade lethality (measuring effectiveness via sovereign spread widening speed and leading enterprises' market capitalisation evaporation rate). Research indicates this model systematically circumvents existing collective defence frameworks: actions may superficially appear as industrial accidents or public order issues, making it difficult to trigger countermeasures from military entities at the alliance level. Yet capital markets instantly impose 'credit punishment' on the targeted nation. Consequently, defence priorities shift from preventing isolated disruptions to severing the closed-loop: integrating intelligence, financial regulation, and public clarification into a unified real-time coordination system to pre-emptively identify anomalous positions and synchronised harassment; legally elevating 'infrastructure sabotage + financial arbitrage' to sovereign-level threats; and deploying 'credit firewalls' to suppress beta and constrain SFR, preventing attacks from evolving into replicable profit-driven models.

title: Teleological Consciousness as the Ground of Religious Growth
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Teleological Consciousness as the Ground of Religious Growth
detail.abstract: This essay explains why religiosityas a way of seeing the world and as an institutional form-arises systematically from the structure of human consciousness. The starting point is simple: we are vividly aware of our willing, we are far less aware of the causal chains that produce it. From this asymmetry springs teleology: a bias to ask "what is this for" rather than "how did this come to be" when teleology becomes shared, it condenses into norms and then into religious institutions. The claim is not polemical, religion here is described as a frame that amplifies, stabilizes, and formats antecedent tendencies-an amplifier, not a generator-and therefore changes when conditions change. In this way we preserve the principle of sufficient reason without collapsing meaning into a void.

detail.title: The European Court of Justice as Political Actor in Intergovernmental Coordination

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of Comparative Politics, Volume 17, No. 1. Pp. 5-18

detail.abstract: The European Court of Justice (ECJ) isn't a political actor, nonetheless, can play a role in solving political debates. ECJ makes rulings on political issues decided by EU bodies. Although ECJ has never elaborated a comprehensive political question doctrine, it did decide case-by-case whether a political problem is justiciable from the 1970's up to now. ECJ legally reviews the operation of the Executive on EU and national level. Besides, courts usually refrain from cases of directly political substance because they cannot take over the role of political actors. The aim of the research is to examine how ECJ has tried to balance between these requirements, and in which cases did it shape European intergovernmental relations. The analysis is mainly based on court cases and their political context. Main conclusion of the research is that ECJ can make a valuable contribution to Europe on becoming a real political community.

title: A Dynamic Federalism Test
affiliations: HEC Paris - Finance Department and HEC Paris

detail.title: A Dynamic Federalism Test

publicationDetails.journalName: HEC Paris Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Federalism notoriously struggles with the allocation of competences between the federal and sub-federal levels. Legal doctrines vary across jurisdictions in how they allocate authority. From an efficiency perspective, the allocation is determined through a "federalism test" comparing the efficiency of each level of government. This comparison is difficult because which allocation will be more efficient in the future is uncertain and potentially endogenous to the current allocation. We formally define efficiency in such a context, show that a "static" federalism test that neglects endogeneity can fail to implement the efficient allocation, and propose a "dynamic" test to address the issue. We discuss the relevance of our results in light of jurisprudence in different policy areas.

detail.title: Extract from the Book: State of the Art in Structured Products

detail.abstract: This paper provides an extract from the book 'State of the Art in Structured Products: Fundamentals, Designing, Pricing, and Hedging' (Advanced Education in Financial Engineering, 2022, 356 pages). The book aims to provide both the theoretical background and the practical applications of structured products in modern financial markets. It systematically explores the fundamentals of derivatives, equity and interest rate markets, stochastic calculus, Monte Carlo simulations, Constant Proportion Portfolio Insurance (CPPI), risk management, and the financial engineering processes involved in designing, pricing, and hedging structured products. This extract includes the preface, table of contents, and introduction of the book. It presents the pedagogical philosophy, structure, and target audience, including graduate students in finance, university professors, and practitioners in derivatives and structured products.

title: Trump Energy Policy 2.0
affiliations: , University of Utah - S.J. Quinney College of Law and University of Utah

detail.title: Trump Energy Policy 2.0

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no financial relationship related to this paper.

detail.abstract:
The second Trump administration has adopted an energy policy with strong echoes from the first administration but sharp departures as well: new wrinkles, different dimensions, and changes in approach. The new policy is more reactionary to the unfolding energy transition, particularly climate regulatory efforts adopted during the Biden administration. It is also more intrepid, invoking sweeping emergency authorities, circumventing longstanding environmental protections, and implementing the policy directly under a much stronger unitary executive theory than in the first administration. Many will welcome President Trump’s effort to reshape the energy landscape. Others are far less sanguine.

Understanding what Trump energy policy 2.0 is and how it will be implemented is thus vital—to industry, the public, state and local governments, and everyone affected by how energy is produced, delivered, and used in the United States. Here, we explain what this policy entails, tracing its contours and mapping how it will be implemented over the next four years. Our contributions are threefold. We describe the policy and contextualize it, both in contrast to the first Trump energy policy and in the current political milieu. We detail how the second Trump administration plans to implement the policy, identifying key actions taken to date. Finally, we identify primary impediments the administration is likely to face as it seeks to give its policy effect.

title: Stanisław Lem's Novel 'Solaris': An Exploration Through the 'Radical Orthodoxy' Categories
affiliations: MGIMO University of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation

detail.title: Stanisław Lem's Novel 'Solaris': An Exploration Through the 'Radical Orthodoxy' Categories
detail.abstract: The author aims to explore the concept of representation and univocality as perceived by John Milbank and the “Radical Orthodoxy” thought through the prism of Stanislaw Lem’s novel “Solaris”. The critical comparison of the diminished and God’s representation principle in Scottist perspective (according to Milbank, fostering secularization and modernity) and the image of the Ocean as depicted by Lem helps to visualize the novel’s religious narrative and unveil its problematic aspects. In this view the paper evokes Christian philosophy as a constructive response to the deadlocks of positivism and secularism resulting in fragmented ontology that leads to virtualization and absurdity. The article reflects how Lem juxtaposes the nature of divine intellect and scientific limitations addressing the challenges posed by Stanislaw Lem’s atheistic worldview, selfcontradictory in advocating for the sacredness and comprehensiveness of science while demonstrating its limitations. Overall, the article provides a distinctive exploration of philosophical and theological themes within Solaris, offering critical insights into the representation of being and its implications within a complex, turbulent ethical landscape. The author suggests further exploration of Lem’s philosophy through the theological lens, particularly in relation to the concept of ‘“firstcontact” novel’.

title: A 360-Degree View of the New Normal: Challenges and Opportunities for a Local University and College in the Philippines
affiliations: Bulacan State University

detail.title: A 360-Degree View of the New Normal: Challenges and Opportunities for a Local University and College in the Philippines
detail.abstract: Abstract: Background:            With the end of the COVID-19 pandemic "in sight" (WHO, 2022), schools in the Philippines are now pivoting back to hybrid, hyperflex, and/or full-on-site classes. School leaders are seen to be key players in the critical and constant evaluation and re-evaluation of teaching and learning strategies, ensuring effective knowledge transfer. Purpose of the study:            This study aimed to identify the challenges and opportunities brought by the new normal in education in a Local University and College in Bulacan, a province in the Philippines, using phenomenography as the qualitative research approach.            Methodology:The study interviewed twelve individuals who met specific inclusion criteria, including technical-vocational and hospitality management students, instructors, parents, and school leaders, to understand the challenges and opportunities of the new normal in education. The study identified six dimensions of learning, referred to as the "outcome space," which can serve as a basis for developing an adaptable pedagogical leadership plan. The study highlights the importance of agility, adaptability, resilience, continuous learning, and inclusive and practical educational approaches. The study recommends that school leaders implement a pedagogical leadership plan addressing these areas to create a resilient and adaptive learning environment that meets the needs of all students. The study used an exploratory approach, with interviews to generate themes related to the six dimensions of learning identified in the outcome space.The authors’ study, "The Dimensions of Learning: A Pedagogical Leadership Plan in the New Normal Education," was developed to address the obstacles to learning in the new normal education environment. The study implies that success in changing education depends on adaptability, resilience, and openness to new approaches.

title: Securing Low-Power Edge AI: A Vulnerability Analysis and Cybersecurity Framework for Resource-Constrained Devices
affiliations: The University of North Carolina at Charlotte,  and 4Sphere Software Solutions LLC, Ramdeobaba University

detail.title: Securing Low-Power Edge AI: A Vulnerability Analysis and Cybersecurity Framework for Resource-Constrained Devices
detail.abstract: The rapid deployment of Edge AI systems powered by low-power technology has created new operational challenges in healthcare facilities, autonomous vehicles, and industrial IoT devices, leading to increased security vulnerabilities. Security mechanisms require strong computational power, which these efficiency and real-time-oriented systems do not possess by design. Predictable threats against Edge AI systems are now more prevalent due to their limited computing power. Security frameworks prove inefficient when used in Edge AI environments, creating a vital protection weakness. This research paper focuses on a new lightweight cybersecurity system designed for Edge AI systems that lack sufficient resources. The proposed security construct enables the deployment of effective cryptographic systems and AI-based anomaly identification along with defence mechanisms suitable for real-time edge devices operating with restricted power consumption. A realistic dataset, known as the Cyber Threat Detection Dataset, was utilised to test the framework, which incorporated multiple normal and attack behaviours, as well as several different attack varieties. The highspeed intrusion detection system relies on Random Forest (RF), while a Lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) handles anomaly detection activities within the framework, and Federated Learning (FL) decentralises learning across different edge nodes with privacy protection. According to test results, the developed framework delivers advanced threat detection accuracy, better energy efficiency, and faster inference speeds. Each security model partakes specific capabilities that enhance a layered defence, resulting in a protected, adaptable and scalable protection for Edge AI systems.

Intelligence In Decentralized Finance
affiliations: , Independent researcher and William Paterson University, William Paterson University

detail.title:
A Systematic Review on the Application of Artificial

Intelligence In Decentralized Finance
detail.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive systematic review of the rapidly evolving field of Decentralized Finance (DeFi) and the crucial role that Artificial Intelligence (AI) plays within it. Using a PRISMAguided search strategy, 39 peer-reviewed articles were identified and analyzed. Key areas of AI application in DeFi are classified as fraud detection, smart contract security, market prediction, credit risk assessment, and governance. The review synthesizes the findings, detailing the AI techniques employed (e.g., machine learning, deep learning, graph neural networks, reinforcement learning, and natural language processing) and assesses their demonstrated performance. Emerging trends and challenges (such as data scarcity, real-time processing, cross-chain integration, and interpretability) are also discussed. The analysis shows that AI has moved beyond an auxiliary role to become an indispensable component for managing DeFi's permissionless, immutable environment. AI's strengths in pattern recognition, anomaly detection, and predictive analytics are presented as essential for building trust and stability in this new financial paradigm. Finally, we discuss implications for future research, emphasizing the need for AI to evolve alongside DeFi in order to ensure security, efficiency, and regulatory compliance.

title: The Multi-Quotient Leadership Framework (MQLF) and Leadership Sustainability Index (LSI): Advancing Sustainable Leadership for SMB Organizational Resilience

detail.abstract: This conceptual article proposes the Multi-Quotient Leadership Framework (MQLF) and the Leadership Sustainability Index (LSI) as integrated tools to assess and guide sustainable leadership practices in small and medium-sized businesses (SMBs). Drawing upon theoretical foundations in intelligence theory, emotional intelligence (EQ), spiritual intelligence (SQ), and adversity quotient (AQ), the MQLF offers a four-dimensional model of leadership competency. The LSI is proposed as a metric-based index for assessing leadership's capacity to drive resilience, sustainable performance, and long-term organizational viability. The paper outlines the conceptual model, hypothesized relationships, and a validation protocol involving surveys, structural modeling, and field testing in SMB contexts. The expected contributions include: (a) offering a multi-dimensional measurement tool for leadership sustainability; (b) bridging theory and practice in SMB leadership development; and (c) informing future research and interventions in resilient leadership.

title: The Operable Good: A Civilizational Framework for Sustainable Empathy
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU)

detail.title: The Operable Good: A Civilizational Framework for Sustainable Empathy
detail.abstract: The "Chapter on Cat Population Management" takes stray animal rescue as its entry point, exploring the self-regeneration mechanisms of human civilization at ethical, commercial, and institutional levels through the "Field-Shi" Philosophical Engineering framework. The entire text begins with individually driven actions fueled by emotion, depicting how goodwill evolves from spontaneous empathy into sustainable social systems. The first part clarifies "goodwill" as the structural foundation of civilizational energy, pointing out that rescue is not a utilitarian act but an existential praxis that confirms humanity's continued capacity for perception. The second part uses cat cafés, TNR, and social enterprises as examples to analyze the economic models of "energy-efficient compassion" and "Emotional Long-term Bonds," proposing that goodwill can become an investable social asset. The third part returns to the philosophical level, drawing on the ideas of Nussbaum and Arendt to argue that "the fragility of the good" and "the narrative nature of praxis" are key to the continuation of civilization. The entire text concludes with the concept of "Bodhicitta," suggesting that the breath of civilization originates from an individual's gentle intention-even just laying down a dry cloth or putting out a bowl of water is maintaining the minimum-power operation of civilization. The book uses stray animal rescue as a symbol, but in reality, it discusses how humanity can maintain the ability for "civilization still breathing" in an era of accelerating technology and cooling emotions through structural goodwill.

title: Data-Driven Bundling with Driver Preferences in Crowd-Sourced Logistics
affiliations: , National University of Singapore and Michigan State University – The Eli Broad College of Business

detail.title: Data-Driven Bundling with Driver Preferences in Crowd-Sourced Logistics
detail.abstract: The surge in e-commerce transactions has posed a major challenge for retail and logistics companies to meet growing customer demand for faster delivery. Crowd-sourced logistics, which leverages local, non-professional couriers (occasional drivers) for parcel delivery, has emerged as an alternative to relying on dedicated fleets. In practice, crowdsourced delivery platforms design jobs to balance efficiency and driver participation, often by bundling multiple parcels into a single delivery job. However, existing bundling strategies, typically based on geographical partition heuristics, do not explicitly model occasional drivers' preferences, leading to low selection rates, reduced service quality, and heavier workloads for dedicated drivers. This paper proposes a data-driven bundling strategy that integrates bundling decisions with predictive models to capture drivers' choice behaviors. We consider two behavioral types: independence, where bundles are evaluated separately, and substitution, where preference for one bundle affects others. The proposed models are formulated as mixed-integer exponential conic programs for small-scale instances, while approximation methods using second-order relaxations and region-partitioning heuristics enable large-scale implementation. We further introduce optimal strategies for constructing small-capacity bundles. A case study using 400 parcels from a Southeast Asian logistics platform demonstrates a 57.31% improvement in selection probability relative to the company's current strategy. Our findings underscore the importance of incorporating driver preferences when designing bundling strategies in crowd-sourced logistics. Accounting for substitution effects produces more effective bundle configurations that align with driver preferences, allowing logistics platforms to enhance service quality, ease the workload of dedicated drivers, and meet growing expectations for faster delivery.

title: Empowered Mothers, Empowered Generations: The Impact of Women’s Economic Rights
affiliations: Vienna University of Economics and Business and Central European University

detail.title: Empowered Mothers, Empowered Generations: The Impact of Women’s Economic Rights

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper examines the long-run effects of women’s economic rights on generations exposed to property and earnings acts during childhood. We find that childhood exposure to these reforms reduced the probability of marriage—particularly among women—and increased female labor force participation in adulthood. To explore potential mechanisms, we document several short-run effects among the adult generation contemporaneous to the reforms, including improved occupational standing, reduced fertility, lower child mortality, and increased schooling among children. Taken together, our findings suggest that expanding economic rights for women can shape outcomes across multiple generations, underscoring the enduring importance of legal and institutional reforms that promote women’s economic empowerment.

title: The Wage Effects of Restricting Temporary Foreign Workers: Evidence from Canada’s 2014 TFWP Reforms
affiliations: National Taipei University and Memorial University of Newfoundland (MUN) - Department of Economics

detail.title: The Wage Effects of Restricting Temporary Foreign Workers: Evidence from Canada’s 2014 TFWP Reforms

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This study examines the labor market impacts of Canada’s 2014 reforms to the Temporary Foreign Worker Program (TFWP), which introduced stricter limits on hiring low-skilled foreign workers. Using a difference-in-differences framework with Labour Force Survey data from 2005 to 2019, we compare wage outcomes for domestic workers in TFW-intensive occupations to those in similar low-skill jobs unaffected by the reforms. Robustness checks— including event study analysis, propensity score matching, placebo tests, and additional validation with Census data (2006, 2011, 2016)—consistently show that the reforms led to a statistically significant increase in wages for affected domestic workers. The estimated impact ranges from 3.7% to 4.5%, suggesting that restricting access to temporary foreign labor modestly improves wage outcomes for low-wage Canadians. These findings offer timely insights amid renewed policy efforts to tighten immigration, highlighting the potential benefits of targeted reforms while cautioning against broader restrictions that could undermine labor market responsiveness and sectoral needs.

title: Reconstituting Corporate Power & Accountability

detail.title: Reconstituting Corporate Power & Accountability

publicationDetails.detailsText: GWU Law School Public Law Research Paper Forthcoming
publicationDetails.journalName: George Washington University Law School, Public Law & Legal Theory Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Modern society faces a growing crisis of corporate impunity. While corporations generate immense value, they increasingly inflict harm at scales that dwarf those of traditional street crime. Decades of deregulation, unchecked corporate lobbying, and a judiciary actively dismantling the administrative state have created a dangerous accountability vacuum. And just as federal oversight is collapsing, the Supreme Court's expanding preemption doctrine is handcuffing state regulators. This Article proposes a paradigm shift: the revitalization of state criminal authority, a power largely shielded from federal interference. Upon securing a conviction or deferred prosecution agreement, states should mandate that the offending corporation conduct all future business within the state through a public benefit corporation. This innovative remedy moves beyond ineffective fines, leveraging the state's authority over corporate charters to fundamentally restructure corporate incentives and align the pursuit of profit with the public good.

title: Inheritance Shocks and Expenditure Patterns: A Dynamic Collective Approach
affiliations: University of Zaragoza, University of Zaragoza - Department of Economic Analysis and University of Zaragoza

detail.title: Inheritance Shocks and Expenditure Patterns: A Dynamic Collective Approach

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: Understanding how household decisions react to economic shocks is important for effective policy design. Using detailed individual consumption data, we investigate how household consumption responds to unexpected inheritance realizations within an inter-temporal collective framework. Inheritances constitute personal assets that are not equally divided upon divorce among spouses according to matrimonial property laws, and they play the role of stochastic distribution factors affecting intra-household bargaining dynamics. Estimating a dynamic collective model, the analysis provides evidence consistent with dynamic bargaining effects. In particular, heirs immediately increase their consumption growth, while their partners experience a decline in their consumption. These findings are not driven by liquidity- or credit-constrained households, which could otherwise lead households to overreact to inheritance receipts.

title: Algorithmic Governance For Water Management During Climate Change-Related Droughts: A Working Paper

detail.title: Algorithmic Governance For Water Management During Climate Change-Related Droughts: A Working Paper
detail.abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has been increasingly introduced as a tool to support decision-making and strategies for responding to climate change-related droughts. Within this context, the PhD project presented here examines the effects of so-called algorithmic governance on social structures, such as social categorisation and governance strategies, when AI is integrated into water management. A case study conducted in Catalonia (Spain) provides empirical data. The AI application analysed consist in smart meters (incorporating AI-based technologies) installed in households to monitor water usage during drought scenarios. Qualitative and participatory methodologies are being implemented, as well as the development of an agent-based model (ABM) which aims to explore “what-if” scenarios including different top-down and bottom-up governance strategies.

title: Casting a Long Shadow: How Parental Risky Behaviors Impair Child Development in Russia
affiliations: University of Perugia, University of Verona and Free University of Bozen-Bolzano

detail.title: Casting a Long Shadow: How Parental Risky Behaviors Impair Child Development in Russia

publicationDetails.journalName: IZA Institute of Labor Economics Discussion Paper Series

detail.abstract: This paper estimates the short-run impact of parental risky behaviors on multiple dimensions of child development using 30 years of data from a representative Russian longitudinal survey. We use factor analysis to construct a composite index of parental risky behaviors and health habits. The panel nature of the data allows us to implement individual and household fixed-effects models, which control for all time-invariant unobserved heterogeneity that might correlate with both parenting and child outcomes. We find that exposure to parental risky behaviors adversely affects childrens educational attainment (grade-for-age) and increases their propensity for risky behaviors, specifically smoking and drinking. Conversely, we find no significant impact on soft skills and only weak evidence of negative health outcomes. These impacts are more pronounced for older children and those in higher-income households.

title: Breathing on the Wrong Side: The Health Costs of Downwind Exposure to Road Traffic
affiliations: Xiamen University - School of Economics, Xiamen University, Xiamen University and Xiamen University

detail.title: Breathing on the Wrong Side: The Health Costs of Downwind Exposure to Road Traffic
detail.abstract: This paper examines how daily variation in downwind exposure to traffic pollutants affects residents' health, using smartphone records to track hospital visits. A one-standard-deviation increase in downwind exposure raises hospital visits and stay duration by 0.11% and 1.96%, respectively, primarily driven by NO 2. Health impacts are more pronounced for vulnerable age groups, particularly children and the elderly. We find no evidence of sorting behavior to avoid downwind exposure. Subway openings mitigate these adverse health effects, which translates into annual health expenditure savings over $100 million, equating to 2.2% of the city's yearly medical spending, highlighting sizable public health gains from public-transit infrastructure.

title: Development of "JOB Labor Market Card Game", an Instructional Tool in Labor Economics Course
affiliations: and INTI International University

detail.title: Development of "JOB Labor Market Card Game", an Instructional Tool in Labor Economics Course
detail.abstract: Traditional pedagogy in economics education often struggles with the abstract and quantitative nature of the subject that can lead to diminished student engagement and comprehension. This study addresses that pedagogical challenge by developing and evaluating the "JOB Labor Market Card Game," an innovative instructional tool for labor economics course. Employing a mixed-method research design, the researchers assessed the game's effect on student learning and engagement. The research population consisted of 47 undergraduate economics students at Pangasinan State University. Descriptive statistics and Chi-square tests were used for quantitative analysis to measure the game's acceptability across three dimensions: attention, relevance, and satisfaction. Thematic analysis was employed for qualitative data. The results reveal a very high level of acceptability for the game, with mean scores consistently above 4.35 on a 5-point Likert scale. Students reported improvements in motivation, active participation, and comprehension of complex labor market concepts. The game was perceived as a valuable supplement to traditional teaching methods that can enhance analytical, social, and decision-making skills. Qualitative data reinforced these findings which suggest that the game has the ability to make learning more interactive and engaging. The study concludes that the integration of educational games such as the developed "JOB" Labor Maret Card Game is a valuable and effective supplement to conventional teaching methods in economics and other complex disciplines in higher education.

detail.title: The Role of Regulation in Information Systems Research -A Conceptual Framework

declarations.funderStatement: This research has received funding from the Research Council of Finland (AI-REG project, grant number 347221) and the Strategic Research Council of the Research Council of Finland (TRANSFORM-AI, grant number 372921).

publicationDetails.detailsText: Australasian Conference on Information Systems (ACIS), Dec 3-5, 2025, Brisbane, Australia.

detail.abstract: Legally binding regulations greatly influence the development and use of information technology (IT) and information systems (IS), with many rules governing IT artifacts. Consequently, IS research has engaged in studying regulation for decades, and in recent years, this focus has surged. However, prevailing conceptualizations of regulation-related IS research, while diverse, often oversimplify the multifaceted nature of this phenomenon, making it difficult to fully understand its implications and impacts on both theory and practice. To clarify the diverse conceptualizations and relationships at play, we provide a framework, based on our ongoing literature review, outlining eight ways in which IS research has conceptually acknowledged the relationship between legally binding regulation and other phenomena. We advance IS research in two ways: by enhancing the conceptual understanding of regulation beyond existing classifications, and by identifying key questions from our framework to guide further inquiry into regulation's role in IS research.

title: Monetary Policy Transmission: A Reference Guide Through ESCB Models and Empirical Benchmarks

detail.title: Monetary Policy Transmission: A Reference Guide Through ESCB Models and Empirical Benchmarks

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Occasional Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: This paper serves as a reference guide on the effects of “standard” monetary policy shocks on output and prices, based on harmonised simulation exercises conducted across models of the European System of Central Banks (ESCB), meta-analysis of existing empirical literature for the euro area, and selected works on heterogeneity and non-linearities in the monetary transmission mechanism as captured by empirical models. Our analysis starts by comparing the effects of monetary policy shocks as estimated by structural, semi-structural and dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models, and identifying the main sources of heterogeneity – most notably via the specification of monetary policy rules, the slope of the Phillips curve, the role of real rigidities and financial frictions, and the expectations formation mechanism. While DSGE models tend to produce sharper responses, semi-structural models often reveal more gradual and persistent effects, in line with backward-looking empirical models. The second chapter presents a meta-analysis of estimated effects based on the empirical literature, which are broadly consistent with the results obtained from the ESCB models, although differences might appear when correcting for publication bias, or accounting for different identification frameworks. The study is then complemented by selected works on heterogeneity and non-linearities in the monetary transmission mechanism as captured by empirical models. Our analysis in the final chapter shows that monetary policy transmission is heterogeneous across countries, sectors, demand components, and time. It also reveals important non-linear and state-dependent dynamics: in high-inflation periods, greater price and wage flexibility amplifies the response of inflation while dampening output effects, thereby lowering the sacrifice ratio.
