title: Workplace Values and Employee Engagement in the Public Sector: Foundations for Strategic Organizational Development
affiliations: , , , World Citi Colleges - Quezon City - Graduate School Department and World Citi Colleges - Quezon City - Graduate School Department

detail.title: Workplace Values and Employee Engagement in the Public Sector: Foundations for Strategic Organizational Development

declarations.ethicsApproval: All participants provided informed consent prior to their inclusion in the study, and their anonymity and confidentiality were strictly maintained throughout the research process.

detail.abstract: This comprehensive systematic literature review synthesizes global and Philippine scholarship on workplace values and employee engagement within public sector organizations. Anchored in Super's Work Values Inventory and Gallup's Q12 engagement framework, the review follows a PRISMA-informed methodology and addresses four objectives: identifying predominant work values across core values, environment, interactions, and activities; assessing engagement levels across basic needs, individual contribution, teamwork, and growth; analyzing relationships between individual work values and engagement dimensions; and recommending strategies for aligning organizational practice with employee values to strengthen engagement. The synthesis integrates theoretical models including person–organization fit, social exchange theory, self-determination theory, and job demands-resources model to explain mechanisms linking values and engagement. The review concludes with a detailed strategic alignment framework and a fillable template for future empirical use in Philippine public agencies.

title: Subway Construction, Café Talks, and Innovation
affiliations: School of Economics, Xiamen University, Xiamen University and Department of Finance at School of Economics (SOE),  and Wang Yanan Institute for Studies in Economics (WISE), Xiamen University

detail.title: Subway Construction, Café Talks, and Innovation
detail.abstract: This paper examines how urban infrastructure reshapes informal social spaces and thus, innovation. Using data on Dianping (similar to Yelp in the U. S.) from 2013 to 2022, we show that café density increases significantly within a 1.4 km of new subway stations in China. Employing a stacked difference-indifferences design, we find that the invention applications increase by 8.93% following subway openings. Decomposition analysis further shows that subway-induced cafés account for 39.2% of the observed innovation gains, primarily driven by the top-tier inventors, intra-firm patents, and newly established collaborations. Smartphone mobility records reveal that cafés near new stations lengthen visit durations and increase informal meetings among inventors. These findings suggest that subways stimulate local innovation output by facilitating more frequent face-to-face interactions in newly accessible third places.

title: Decentralization in Somaliland

detail.title: Decentralization in Somaliland
detail.abstract: The main goal of decentralization is to shift power away from the national government and toward local or subnational ones. Based on the Somaliland context, this article highlights the decentralization of the administrative (de-concentration, delegation, and devolution) political, fiscal, market, and economic spheres. The literature on decentralization in Africa is the main subject of this investigation. especially Somaliland. Two times, Somaliland reclaimed its independence: first, on June 26, 1990, under British protectorate, it joins Somalia on July 1, 1960. Second it was in 18 May1991, the Somali Republic's rule was overthrown by the Somali National Movement (SNM) following a protracted battle by the Somaliland community. On 1991, Somaliland reclaimed their sovereignty. This brief history will demonstrate the various historical administrative decentralizations that Somaliland has seen, beginning in 1951 with the British Protectorate. The theoretical conceptualizations found in the literature were used as a methodology in this study. Several countries including East African nations will be used as examples in this paper, with a focus on devolution and administrative decentralization. This paper will also provide you with an additional understanding of how Somaliland upholds democracy and permits its citizens to engage and utilize their rights throughout the nation. All the points that these paper covers will base Somaliland legal framework. The various notions of decentralization, inclusive administrative decentralization, political decentralization, fiscal decentralization, market and economic decentralization, and other concepts under the key concepts are finally explained and presented in this study.

title: Supply Chain Triangulation: A Digital-Resilience Architecture Across Nodes, Data, and Analytics
affiliations: Global Supply Chain

detail.title: Supply Chain Triangulation: A Digital-Resilience Architecture Across Nodes, Data, and Analytics
detail.abstract: Supply chains face simultaneous shocks from demand volatility, geopolitical fragmentation, and carbon constraints. We propose Supply Chain Triangulation (SCT) as an integrative architecture that couples (i) physical triangulation (multi-node sourcing/fulfilment across suppliers, DCs, stores, and 3PLs), (ii) informational triangulation (fusion of demand, inventory, logistics, and external signals), and (iii) computational triangulation (hybrid analytics spanning AI/ML, simulation, and optimization) to maximize resilience and minimize cost-to-serve and emissions. We formalize SCT as a multiobjective control problem balancing service, cost, and CO₂, and show how digital-twin implementations and multi-objective routing (e.g., Pollution Routing Problem variants) operationalize the approach at scale. We map SCT to viability theory (resilience + adaptability + sustainability) and "de-risking" debates, arguing that diversified, triangulated networks outperform single-sourcing and pure reshoring on viability and welfare metrics. We synthesize methods (MinT reconciliation, GNN/transformers for forecasting, ALNS/tabu for VRP, and green VRP formulations) and outline a research and practice agenda: metrics (Triangulation Resilience Index), benchmark datasets, and policy-aware design. The contribution is a unifying language and toolkit that researchers and practitioners can reuse across inventory, routing, finance, and policy contexts, accelerating cumulative scholarship and deployment.

title: Building a Purpose of the Company: Friedman and Freeman as Beacons in a Pragmatist Theory of the Firm
affiliations: Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Building a Purpose of the Company: Friedman and Freeman as Beacons in a Pragmatist Theory of the Firm

publicationDetails.detailsText: Business Ethics Quarterly, volume 35, issue 3, 2025[10.1017/beq.2024.21]

detail.abstract: When considering the implications of the shareholder-stakeholder debate in defining the purpose of a company, epistemological clarity is vital in this emerging theory of the firm. Such clarity can prevent recurrence based solely on rephrasing key terms. To understand how various stakeholders develop and interpret a shared purpose, I argue for the necessity of a pragmatist approach that is normative and process-oriented. Mental models play a crucial role in interpretive processes that define decision-making, where individual perspectives converge. The figures of Milton Friedman and Ed Freeman serve as "beacons," as artefacts, in the transmission of knowledge through which we, as individuals, shape a shared understanding. In current societies, profound polarization obstructs solutions to grand challenges. Pragmatism starts by questioning the underlying values of everyone involved. It assumes that sound deliberative processes are the only way to reach real solutionsnot only for the mind but, above all, for the heart. title: When the Lights Go Out: A Nowcasting Framework for Labor and Output During Federal Data Blackouts
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: When the Lights Go Out: A Nowcasting Framework for Labor and Output During Federal Data Blackouts
detail.abstract: The October 2025 U.S. federal shutdown halted the regular collection and dissemination of economic statistics from key agencies including the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS), the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), and the Census Bureau. This paper proposes a theoretical and empirical nowcasting framework for inferring real-time labor and output conditions when official data are unavailable. The model combines private and state-level indicators-ADP private payrolls, online vacancies (HWOL/Indeed), initial unemployment insurance claims, electricity load proxies for industrial activity, and consumer sentimentto estimate latent employment and output. We formalize a state-space representation with a shutdown shock and design a validation plan using pre-shutdown data. We discuss limitations, identification risks, and policy implications for building redundant statistical infrastructure. Illustrative simulations show how longer shutdowns can amplify labor stress and reduce quarterly GDP growth in line with existing estimates.

title: Unsupervised PCA Framework for Heatwave Vulnerability with Perturbation-Based Robustness Validation
affiliations: Independent and Independent

detail.title: Unsupervised PCA Framework for Heatwave Vulnerability with Perturbation-Based Robustness Validation
detail.abstract: This paper introduces an unsupervised machine learning approach to quantifying heatwave vulnerability based on principal component analysis (PCA) modeling. Investigating the case study of Memphis, Tennessee, the paper aims to propose a replicable machine learning architecture to generate interpretable latent structures from high-dimensional indicators. The model projected 22 neighborhood socioeconomic factors, extracted through U.S. census data for 27 neighborhoods, into reduced orthogonal feature space to produce four principal components (PCs). PCA was successful in explaining approximately 85% of total variance in neighborhood data. The PCs (PC1-PC4) were also grouped into four meaningful broad socioeconomic sectors based on top loading factors, representing workforce mobility, aging urban density, housing diversity, and developing infrastructure indexes, respectively. A composite vulnerability index (scaled 1-100) was devised with the strategic summation of the PCs weighted by respective explained variance ratios (EVRs). A key methodology, sensitivity analysis, was developed to test the robustness of the machine learning model in two ways. EVRs of each PC were shocked in isolation by ±10%, ±20%, ±30%. PC1 and PC2 were the most sensitive, with vulnerability scores shifting by 8.29%-49.03%. Stochastic noise perturbation was performed by adding a Gaussian noise of 10% the original standard deviation to gauge the sensitivity of loading factors by PC. PC3 and PC4 feature-PC combinations were the most sensitive, with the highest absolute mean shifts in loading factors in the range of 0.49-0.58 (mainly housing diversity and green space proportion variables). Despite these variations, vulnerability and loading factor rankings remained robust, supporting PCA as an effective baseline model. In future work, supervised machine learning techniques like ensemble random forest or XGBoost models can be evaluated to benchmark PCA results.

title: Warning Cultures in Practice : Shadow Systems in Local Flood Risk Governance
affiliations: University of Reading, University of Reading, University of Reading and University of Reading

detail.title: Warning Cultures in Practice : Shadow Systems in Local Flood Risk Governance
detail.abstract: Early warning reduces flood risk when forecasts are interpreted and converted into timely local action. In Luxembourg, a nationally centralised system, with no intermediate tier, places the next line of decision making immediately with municipalities. This paper examines how a structured shadow system emerges at the local scale to bridge gaps between national alerts and operational needs. Thematic analysis shows that national flood alerts are generic, repetitive, and weakly linked to municipal thresholds for initiating preparedness measures. Ambiguous terminology, colour codes, and broad spatial and temporal framing limit their operational usefulness for local response. Frequent low-level alerts contribute to warning fatigue and erode trust. Officials construct meaning through institutional knowledge, lived experience, peer exchange, and heuristics. These locally embedded practices highlight the importance of scale, showing how municipal knowledge both localises and at times overrides national messages. The configuration strengthens local responsiveness but concentrates interpretive responsibility at municipal level without formal support, which can increase variability across jurisdictions. The analysis points to a need for impact-based, temporally precise, municipality-scale products with clear triggers and guidance co-developed with local officials and potentially residents, so that centrally issued forecasts can be converted into anticipatory action at the local level.

title: Moving-Block Based Lane-Sharing Strategy for Autonomous-rail Rapid Transit with a Leading Eco-Driving Approach
affiliations: Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University, Southwest Jiaotong University and Southwest Jiaotong University

detail.title: Moving-Block Based Lane-Sharing Strategy for Autonomous-rail Rapid Transit with a Leading Eco-Driving Approach
detail.abstract: Autonomous-rail Rapid Transit (ART) systems operate on standard roadways while maintaining dedicated right-of-way privileges. Owing to their sustainability, punctual operation, and cost efficiency, ART systems have emerged as a promising solution for medium-capacity urban transit. However, the exclusive lane usage for ART systems frequently leads to inefficient lane utilization, thereby intensifying congestion for non-ART vehicles. This study proposes a moving-block based lane-sharing strategy for ART with a leading eco-driving approach. First, dynamic lane-access rules are introduced, allowing non-ART vehicles to temporarily use the ART lane without forced clearance or signal coordination. Second, a modified eco-driving trajectory optimization algorithm is developed for ART, which not only provides stop-free trajectories but also guides following vehicles toward energy-efficient driving behaviors. Finally, simulation experiments are conducted to evaluate the impacts of traffic demand, arrival interval, and non-ART vehicles compliance rate on system performance. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly reduces delay and energy consumption for non-ART vehicles by 72.6% and 24.6%, respectively, without compromising ART operations efficiency. This work provides both technical insights and theoretical support for the efficient management of ART systems and the sustainable development of urban transportation.

title: CCPPO: Reinforcement Learning enhancing confidence for object detection in industrial environments
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: CCPPO: Reinforcement Learning enhancing confidence for object detection in industrial environments
detail.abstract: The proliferation of autonomous systems in industrial and warehousing environments necessitates highly reliable object detection, yet these settings present significant challenges, including severe occlusions, variable illumination, and the prevalence of extremely small objects. Standard deep learning detectors struggle in these high-variance scenes, as their inherent confidence scores are often unreliable, which is unacceptable for safety-critical applications like obstacle avoidance. Furthermore, any viable solution must explicitly satisfy near real-time inference latency constraints. Addressing this gap, this paper introduces Context Confidence Proximal Policy Optimization (CCPPO), a novel reinforcement learning (RL)–based algorithm designed to enhance detector robustness. CCPPO exploits contextual and domain-specific information—reasoning often absent from contemporary neural approaches—to evaluate and refine model predictions. Operating either as a complement to or a replacement for the conventional confidence function, CCPPO leverages RL, analogous to its use in refining Large Language Model outputs, to provide a more assured measure of certainty. We demonstrate the substantial benefits of this approach on the challenging LOCO dataset, showing that  CCPPO significantly improves detection performance while maintaining inference latencies compatible with stringent industrial requirements.

title: Collective Action in Digital Communities: What Drives Active Online Participation?
affiliations: Singapore-ETH Centre, , ,  and

detail.title: Collective Action in Digital Communities: What Drives Active Online Participation?
detail.abstract: Digital platforms are increasingly used to address and solve local community problems, hereby fostering civic engagement and promoting social resilience. Yet, the drivers of residents’ active participation in such spaces are often not sufficiently clear. This study examines the roles of platform governance as well as social, psychological, and digital factors in shaping active participation in online problem-solving communities. Using a mixed-methods design, we ran a four-week online community experiment testing the effects of varying platform governance structures (democratic vs. autocratic) and a cross-sectional survey assessing social, psychological and digital predictors of participation. While the experiment found no significant difference in participation levels between governance types, our survey results reveal that social identity, social norms, and self-efficacy are the strongest predictors of participation. Participants who reported a strong sense of group belonging and perceived clear social expectations were more likely to post, comment, and vote digitally. Collective efficacy was found to be negatively associated with active participation, indicating that high group confidence may diffuse individual responsibility. Digital factors such as digital literacy and perceived surveillance showed no significant effects, suggesting that access and awareness alone do not guarantee engagement. Our findings extend findings from existing models of collective problem-solving and offers recommendations for how to use digital platforms to activate residents’ engagement.  Strengthening individual efficacy and cultivating social connectivity (represented by social identity and norms) seems to be more effective than platform governance interventions.

title: Learning to Group for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing Optimization
affiliations: Anhui University, Anhui University, Anhui University and Hefei Comprehensive National Science Center

detail.title: Learning to Group for Large-Scale Vehicle Routing Optimization
detail.abstract: The large-scale capacitated vehicle routing problem poses a significant logistical challenge due to the vast solution space. Existing heuristic algorithms often employ grouping methods to decompose the problem into smaller sub-problems, thereby reducing the search space. However, they seldom consider both customer distribution and solution structural characteristics simultaneously for refined grouping, which significantly impacts algorithm performance. To address this issue, this paper introduces a heuristic algorithm based on learning-driven dynamic grouping. This algorithm leverages a learning method to dynamically group customers during the search process, integrating solution structure information and considering the intricate interactions between customers and vehicles. Specifically, an attention model is designed to capture not only the distribution information of customers but also the structural information of solutions for dynamic grouping. Furthermore, a new decoding strategy is proposed to facilitate the allocation of customers to vehicles. The performance of the proposed algorithm is validated using test instances from real-world datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm is well-suited for various distributions of large-scale routing problems and offers high computational efficiency.

title: Philosophy or Philosophizing? The Learning Objectives Of Philosophy Programs For Managers
affiliations: University of Fribourg

detail.title: Philosophy or Philosophizing? The Learning Objectives Of Philosophy Programs For Managers
detail.abstract: Many scholars propose philosophy programs as an effective mode of educating, training and developing managers. However, it remains unclear how philosophy could add value to management learning; the intended learning outcomes of such programs are undocumented and little is known about their aims. To better understand philosophy’s potential contribution to management education, training and development, this study investigates the learning objectives of over 60 programs across 22 countries. In a series of semi-structured interviews with professors and trainers who teach philosophy to managers, I discovered why philosophy programs are taught in business contexts. One of the key findings is that most educators avoid teaching ‘philosophy’ as a discipline, but rather teach ‘philosophizing’ as a method. I also identified six distinct categories which outline the learning objectives of philosophy for management programs. These include: personal development, brain training, interpretation and articulation, tolerance and acceptance of differences, managerial competency development, and mystery. This paper provides a better understanding of how philosophy aspires to add value to the field of management learning based on a teaching paradigm. It also instructs pedagogues on how they can approach philosophical teaching in a manner that is relevant to managers.

title: Consumers' environmental awareness and endogenous timing game with environmental corporate social responsibility
affiliations: Dalian Maritime University, Dalian Maritime University and Chonnam National University

detail.title: Consumers' environmental awareness and endogenous timing game with environmental corporate social responsibility
detail.abstract: This study considers the effects of consumers’ environmental awareness (CEA) on polluting firm’s strategic environmental corporate social responsibility and examines an endogenous timing game in mixed and private duopolies under quantity and price competition, respectively. Under quantity competition, firms move simultaneously (sequentially) when CEA is low (high) in a mixed duopoly, while they always move simultaneously in a private duopoly. Under price competition, firms choose their prices sequentially (simultaneously) when CEA is low (high) in both mixed and private duopolies. We also find that privatization consistently reduces welfare regardless of the competition mode and CEA. Finally, when the government can commit to no privatization, firms can endogenously agree to simultaneous-move price competition if CEA is sufficiently high, which can solve the conflict of interests, while government’s further intervention is important to maintain public price leadership if CEA is low. Our findings suggest that green education paired with public leadership can promote the welfare-improving reconfiguration of firms’ choices of competition timing.

title: Multiscale physics-informed modeling and hybrid intelligent control of urban district heating networks
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Zhejiang University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Multiscale physics-informed modeling and hybrid intelligent control of urban district heating networks
detail.abstract: District heating (DH) networks exhibit strong multi-physics coupling, transport delays, and user heterogeneity that complicate prediction and control. This study develops a physics-constrained, multi-scale state-space model of the primary–secondary network, plate heat exchanger, buried twin-pipes, and room/building thermal dynamics, and couples it with a hybrid Temporal Convolutional Network-Fuzzy Cognitive Map (TCN-FCM) predictor whose hyperparameters are globally tuned by the Black Kite Algorithm (BKA). A prediction-driven Proportional–Integral–Derivative (PID) controller is then tuned using the Whale Optimization Algorithm (WOA) to coordinate primary-side valve opening. The framework is validated on a real DH system serving 28 buildings (153,000 m2) over an entire heating season. Thermal-hydraulic simulation accurately reproduces secondary-loop behavior (return temperature errors concentrated within ±0.2°C; supply mostly within ±0.3°C). For short-term (48 h) forecasting, the BKA-TCN-FCM achieves RMSE = 0.350, MAE = 0.280, and MAPE = 0.58%, outperforming ablations and benchmarks, including TCN-Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), TCN-Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), and TCN-Support Vector Regression (SVR). For medium-term (160 h) horizons, it sustains robust accuracy (RMSE = 0.393, MAE = 0.335, MAPE = 0.70%). Closed-loop tests show that the WOA-PID delivers rapid responses with effective overshoot suppression and small steady-state error; over 48 h and 160 h windows, valve actuation remains closely synchronized with supply temperature, which is maintained within a narrow band (≈47.6-48.4oC). By fusing physical constraints, causal interpretability, and metaheuristic optimization, the proposed framework provides an accurate, scalable, and explainable foundation for intelligent DH operation and low-carbon heating.

title: Partners Among Strangers: A Social Relations Perspective on Personality and Collaborative Partner Preferences in First Encounters
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Delft University of Technology, Delft University of Technology, VU University Amsterdam, Delft University of Technology and VU University Amsterdam

detail.title: Partners Among Strangers: A Social Relations Perspective on Personality and Collaborative Partner Preferences in First Encounters
detail.abstract: Collaborative partnerships are often formed following a first encounter. For example, unacquainted individuals may collaborate to complete a project, develop a product, or solve a problem. Using the Social Relations Model, this study examined the extent to which first-encounter trait perceptions predicted collaborative partner preferences. Previously-unacquainted participants (N = 297, 55 groups, 55.9% female) interacted dyadically and provided round-robin ratings of extraversion, honesty-humility, competence, and partner preference. At the target level, individuals who were consistently viewed as extraverted and competent were consistently preferred more as partners. At the relationship level, individuals who were uniquely viewed as honest-humble and competent were uniquely preferred more as partners. Findings underscore the relevance of target- and relationship-specific perceptions in predicting first-encounter collaborative partner preferences.

title: Machining process and parametric geometric characterization of functional edges in valve spools
affiliations: Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology, Harbin Institute of Technology and Harbin Institute of Technology

detail.title: Machining process and parametric geometric characterization of functional edges in valve spools
detail.abstract: Spool valves are extensively employed in servo control systems for aerospace and other engineering applications, where their flow control precision is highly sensitive to the micro-geometry of their functional edges, particularly in small-opening regions. This study investigates the machining and parametric geometric characterization of these edges. Through the measurement of burr dimensions following grinding experiments, the influence of process parameters on burr formation was systematically examined. To address the limitations of manual deburring, this study developed an in-situ deburring device based on constant-force removal and experimentally determined the optimal deburring force. Building on this, a function-oriented parametric characterization method was proposed to link the geometric features of the edge with its operational behavior. The proposed method was further applied to evaluate valve spool edges by measuring the functional edges resulting from both manual and in-situ deburring processes. The results demonstrate that the in-situ deburring process significantly enhances edge quality compared to manual techniques. Moreover, the proposed characterization method offers a quantitative framework for evaluating the micro-geometry of functional edges.

title: The Role of Work-Life-Balance in Effective Business Management
affiliations: Bialystok University of Technology,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, , MAMASTUDIO Pawlik, Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, Bialystok University of Technology, WSB Merito University and ZS "Strzelec" OSW JS 1011 Grajewo

detail.title: The Role of Work-Life-Balance in Effective Business Management
detail.abstract: Purpose: This paper explores the role of work-life balance (WLB) in enhancing employee motivation. It also examines how balancing professional and personal life impacts business management. Design/methodology/approach: The research used a quantitative methodology and an online survey of 102 individuals. It focused on flexible working hours, private medical care, and company cars. Findings: Flexible working hours were the most effective tool for improving WLB. A positive correlation was found between WLB perception and employee motivation. Research limitations/implications: The study is limited to a specific demographic and geographic scope. Future research could explore diverse cultural and occupational contexts. Practical implications: Flexible working hours and private medical care significantly enhance employee satisfaction. These strategies also strengthen employer branding and reduce turnover. Social implications: Promoting WLB can reduce stress and improve societal well-being. Organisations adopting WLB strategies set benchmarks for corporate social responsibility. Originality/value: This study evaluates WLB tools and their impact on employee motivation. It provides valuable insights for HR managers and organisational leaders.

title: National culture and environmental management activism of microfinance institutions
affiliations: University of Chittagong, Curtin University, University of Chittagong, The University of Western Australia and University of Western Australia

detail.title: National culture and environmental management activism of microfinance institutions
detail.abstract: We examine whether national culture is material in the adoption of environmental management strategies in microfinance institutions' (MFIs’) activities. We empirically test a set of hypotheses based on Hofstede’s four national cultural dimensions using an unbalanced panel dataset of 1,139 MFI-year observations from 365 MFIs operating in 26 countries across the period 2007-2018. Our results suggest that uncertainty avoidance is positively associated, and individualism and power distance dimensions are negatively associated with the environmental management activism of MFIs. We also find weak evidence of a negative influence of masculinity on environmental management activism. In addition, we find that the profit orientation of MFIs effects the relationship between national culture and MFI environmental management activism. Our study demonstrates that policy-making bodies, regulatory authorities, and support organizations should consider a country's cultural context when developing policies and standards.

title: Forward Premium Anomaly Resolved
affiliations: Independent Researcher, Qatar University - College of Business and Economics and University of Stirling

detail.title: Forward Premium Anomaly Resolved
detail.abstract: This paper propounds that the Forward Premium Anomaly (FPA) arises due to misspecification in the extant empirical models, where ratios of the concerned variables are studied instead of their levels themselves. We study these variables directly instead of their ratios for 22 currency pairs from both developed and emerging economies and find that the FPA stands resolved for the short-term tenors of weekly and monthly durations. We further conduct tests of cointegration between the dependent and the explanatory variables for the levels and report evidence of cointegration between the variables indicating that their regressions reflect valid relationships.

title: Geopolitical Uncertainty and Firm Default Risk: The Role of Firm Internationalization, Political Exposure, and Industry Affiliation
affiliations: University of Wollongong, Wollongong NSW Australia, University of Wollongong, University of Wollongong, University of Wollongong - School of Accounting, Economics & Finance and University of Wollongong

detail.title: Geopolitical Uncertainty and Firm Default Risk: The Role of Firm Internationalization, Political Exposure, and Industry Affiliation
detail.abstract: Our study examines the relationship between geopolitical risk (GPR) and firm default risk, focusing on the roles of firm internationalization, political exposure, and industry affiliation. Using data from S&P 1500 non-financial firms from 1991 to 2019, we find that heightened GPR significantly increases firm default risk. This relationship remains robust across alternative measures of GPR and default risk, the use of instrumental variables, and the inclusion of macro-level controls. Our path analysis reveals that GPR impacts default risk by depleting cash reserves and raising the cost of debt. Interestingly, we find that firms with higher degree of internationalization (DOI) and political exposure are more vulnerable to default risk during elevated GPR periods, with industry affiliation moderating this effect, as GPR increases default risk only in materials, industrials, consumer staples, health care, IT, and utilities. Finally, we find that heightened default risk during periods of elevated GPR contributes to a decline in firm value. These findings offer critical insights for investors, creditors, and regulators, informing risk management, investment strategies, and policy formulation.

title: Enhanced Graph Entropy via Discrete Wavelet Transform: A Novel Health Index for Early Bearing Fault Detection
affiliations: Shandong University, Shandong University, Taiyuan University of Technology, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Shandong University and Shandong University

detail.title: Enhanced Graph Entropy via Discrete Wavelet Transform: A Novel Health Index for Early Bearing Fault Detection
detail.abstract: Early detection of fault symptoms can provide effective support for ensuring manufacturing performance and mitigating machines maintenance time. However, the ambiguous boundary between healthy operation and incipient fault stages under noisy, non-stationary, and variable working conditions poses signi cant challenges for precise fault detection. While graph-based methods have demonstrated promise in this domain, model redundancy remains a critical is sue that may compromise the robustness of state change detection. To address this limita tion, this paper extends the graph segmentation strategy by introducing node graph entropy to extract fault-related information from graph structures. This approach incorporates node importance quanti cation through entropy-based measurements and selects e ective graph sub structures. To enhance discriminability among critical nodes, this paper integrates discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to inject multi-scale information into node representations, thereby enabling the development of a novel health index: discrete wavelet transform-enhanced graph entropy (DWTEGEn). Leveraging the robustness of this index, this paper establishes a standard deviation-based statistical alarm decision mechanism for bearing fault detection. Comprehensive experiments across diverse operating conditions and datasets including benchmark traversal s and real-world engineering applications, demonstrating the methods efficacy in early fault symptom detection and its substantial potential for industrial deployment.

title: The Impact of Leadership Styles on Project Efficiency
affiliations: I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, National Louis University - Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu, Jagiellonian University, , Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, MAMASTUDIO Pawlik and WSB Merito University

detail.title: The Impact of Leadership Styles on Project Efficiency
detail.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to investigate the impact of various leadership styles on project efficiency within different organizational contexts. It seeks to identify the key leadership behaviors that contribute to the successful attainment of project goals, stakeholder satisfaction, and overall project performance. Design/methodology/approach: Quantitative research using a questionnaire with 100 project professionals. Data analyzed through statistical methods, including Spearman's correlation. Findings: Leadership styles significantly affect project efficiency. Constructive feedback, clear goals, role clarity, and team initiative are key factors. Research limitations/implications: Limited sample size and scope. Future studies should include diverse industries and cultural contexts. Practical implications: Highlights the need for clear communication, feedback, and team empowerment to improve project outcomes. Social implications: Effective leadership fosters trust, collaboration, and employee satisfaction, boosting productivity. Originality/value: Provides empirical evidence on leadership styles' effect on project efficiency, offering actionable insights for managers.

title: The Challenge of Employee Motivation in Business Management
affiliations: Bialystok University of Technology,  I'M Brand Institute sp. z o.o, , National Louis University - Wyższa Szkoła Biznesu, MAMASTUDIO Pawlik, Piotr Mrzygłód Sprzedaż-Marketing-Consulting, F3-TFS sp. z o.o, Bialystok University of Technology and WSB Merito University

detail.title: The Challenge of Employee Motivation in Business Management
detail.abstract:
Purpose: This paper examines the role of employee motivation in effective business management. It also explores the impact of financial and non-financial motivators on employee engagement.

Design/methodology/approach: The research used a quantitative methodology and an online survey of 102 individuals. Statistical analyses, including variance analysis and correlation analysis, were conducted to identify significant patterns and differences in motivation levels.

Findings: Financial motivators, particularly bonuses for achieving targets, were identified as the most effective. Non-financial motivators, such as flexible work schedules and additional days off, also showed high effectiveness in enhancing motivation. Significant differences in motivation levels were observed by gender, age, and length of service.

Research limitations/implications: The study is limited to a specific demographic and geographic scope. Future research could explore diverse cultural and occupational contexts.
Practical implications: Combining financial and non-financial motivators can effectively increase employee satisfaction and engagement.

Social implications: Fostering effective motivation practices contributes to stronger family-company relationships. Companies adopting such strategies set benchmarks for the best workplace.

Originality/value: This study provides insights into the balance of financial and non-financial motivators in shaping employee motivation. It offers actionable recommendations for HR managers and organisational leaders.

title: Urban Agglomeration Niche Analysis from the Perspective of Multi-Flows: A Case Study of the Yangtze River and Pearl River Delta Regions
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Wuhan University, Wuhan University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hohai University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Hohai University, Wuhan University, Zhejiang Academy of Agricultural Sciences and Wuhan University

detail.title: Urban Agglomeration Niche Analysis from the Perspective of Multi-Flows: A Case Study of the Yangtze River and Pearl River Delta Regions
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of urban agglomerations intensifies challenges in resource allocation and regional coordination. This study integrates multi-dimensional flow analysis with niche theory to examine dynamic interactions between the Yangtze River Delta (YRDUA, 27 cities) and Pearl River Delta (PRDUA, 9 cities). Four types of flows—economic service, traffic, population, and information—were fused using a genetic algorithm to optimize their weights.The optimized integrated network achieved a correlation of R2=0.86 with socioeconomic indicators, outperforming equal-weight models by 15%. Results reveal that information and economic flows dominate inter-agglomeration linkages, while traffic and population flows remain constrained by geography. Core cities such as Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen act as diffusive hubs, driving over 70% of cross-regional interactions, whereas peripheral cities like Huizhou and Wuhu exhibit limited connectivity and high resource dependency. Based on ecological niche indicators of centrality and diffusion–aggregation, cities were classified into diffusive, balanced, receptive, and isolated types, uncovering uneven spatial roles and competition–cooperation dynamics. The findings highlight that strengthening transport and digital networks between PRDUA and YRDUA can reduce spatial disparities, promote balanced niche evolution, and foster sustainable cross-regional collaboration.

title: Electricity Price Volatility and Financial Stress: A Time-Frequency Causal Approach Based on Wavelets
affiliations: Hubei University, China Three Gorges University, Hubei University and China Three Gorges University

detail.title: Electricity Price Volatility and Financial Stress: A Time-Frequency Causal Approach Based on Wavelets
detail.abstract: Our study examined the dynamic dependence and causality effects between electricity price volatility and financial stress using a wavelet framework. Using wavelet coherence and wavelet causality analyses, we examined datasets from Germany, France, the UK, the Netherlands, and Belgium spanning the period from 2007 to 2022. These datasets include electricity spot prices, Financial Stress Index, interest rates, stock market index, and exchange rates. Our findings showed this was particularly pronounced strong causal link during periods of economic distress between electricity price volatility and financial stress, which was characterized by crisis dependence, bidirectional, and asymmetric. Additionally, co-movement effects were observed even in normal economic conditions. We identified stock index volatility as the most significant factor influencing electricity price volatility. Notably, country-specific heterogeneity existed due to differences in energy structure and financial development. In Germany, financial stress significantly drove electricity price volatility, while in the UK, the co-movement relationship was robust between these variables. In France, the use of nuclear technologies had mitigated the effect of fluctuations in electricity prices on financial stress, whereas the Netherlands and Belgium exhibited a strong causal relationship during periods of economic distress. Overall, the results contribute to evidence-based policymaking in the energy and economic domains.

title: The Impact of Industrial Robot Adoption on High-Tech Product Exports: Evidence from Belt and Road Countries
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Shanghai University of International Business and Economics

detail.title: The Impact of Industrial Robot Adoption on High-Tech Product Exports: Evidence from Belt and Road Countries
detail.abstract: This study investigates the impact of industrial robot adoption on high-tech product exports among 45 Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) countries from 2005 to 2019, focusing on both intensive and extensive margins. Using an extended gravity model, results show that robot adoption significantly boosts high-tech exports in both margins. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that higher-income countries and those with aging populations benefit more from robot adoption, particularly in the intensive margin of exports. A comparative analysis with non-BRI countries indicates that the BRI enhances the positive effect of robots on high-tech exports. Mechanism analysis further demonstrates that industrial robots improve high-tech exports through the optimization of human capital and increased imports of intermediate goods. These findings support the Belt and Road Initiative and encourage increased robot adoption to enhance export performance and international competitiveness.

title: The African Yield Paradox: A Four-Lever Framework for Soil Carbon Recapitalization
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The African Yield Paradox: A Four-Lever Framework for Soil Carbon Recapitalization
detail.abstract: Despite decades of fertilizer-centric policies, African cereal yields remain low and unresponsive, revealing a fundamental biophysical constraint: the catastrophic depletion of soil organic carbon (SOC). Below functional thresholds (~2–3%), fertilizer efficacy and yield stability collapse, undermining the productivity of agricultural investments. The 2024 Nairobi and 2025 Kampala Declarations mark a pivotal shift from input substitution to integrated soil health, creating an unprecedented window for systemic reform. This paper frames this imperative as soil carbon recapitalization, the active restoration of SOC to ecologically functional and economically productive levels. It proposes an integrated four-lever framework to operationalize this goal: (1) establish SOC as a verifiable national KPI through digital soil mapping and open MRV; (2) deploy an Africa Soil Carbon Facility to de-risk blended finance for SOC outcomes; (3) catalyze a circular bioeconomy producing certified compost and biochar from organic waste; and (4) reorient public subsidies toward performance-based contracts that reward verified SOC gains. This synergistic system, where measurement enables finance, scales supply, and anchors demand, provides an actionable blueprint. Its phased implementation offers a scientifically grounded and politically viable pathway to recapitalize Africa’s soil carbon base, enhance fertilizer efficiency, and secure durable gains in food security and climate resilience.

title: Multidimensional information spillover effects among China’s carbon, energy and stock markets: A dynamic and multilayer network analysis
affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology and Henan University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Multidimensional information spillover effects among China’s carbon, energy and stock markets: A dynamic and multilayer network analysis
detail.abstract: This paper studies the multidimensional information spillover effects among China’s carbon, energy, and stock markets by using a time-varying parameter vector autoregressive model. Additionally, we have constructed multilayer spillover networks to uncover interactions across different spillover dimensions. By employing the event study method, we also analyze the impacts of extreme events on the multidimensional spillover effects. We find that there are significant spillover effects for return, volatility, and extreme risk among China’s carbon, energy, and stock markets, with the stock market being the primary transmitter, and the carbon and energy markets mainly acting as receivers across different dimensions. Meanwhile, the analysis of multilayer information spillover networks reveals distinct topological characteristics for each layer. At last, shocks from extreme events have substantial impacts on these spillover effects. Our findings highlight the importance of considering all potential spillover effects when analyzing market connectedness for policymakers and investors.

title: A delayed Solow model with the CES production function and negative population growth
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and Jagiellonian University

detail.title: A delayed Solow model with the CES production function and negative population growth
detail.abstract: This study investigates the emergence of cyclic behavior within a conventional Solow capital accumulation model. To this end, it introduces  a production delay (i.e., time-to-build), thereby transforming the capital accumulation equation into a delay differential equation (DDE) with delay-dependent coefficients. The proposed model departs from existing Solow-type delay models in four key respects: First, it adopts a Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) production function, focusing on the empirically supported case where the elasticity of substitution is less than one; Second, it ensures consistency between the aggregate (extensive) and per capita (intensive) delayed capital accumulation equations,as implied by the linear homogeneity of the production function; Third, it examines the dynamic effects of both positive and negative population growth, thereby addressing the demographic shift toward negative growth in many advanced economies; Fourth, it applies the classical method developed by Frisch and Holme (1935) for analyzing the delay equations. Through these extensions, the analysis demonstrates that the delayed capital accumulation process can generate complex dynamics, including cyclical fluctuations. The findings highlight that the production delay serves as a primary drive of such cyclical behavior, particularly under the contemporary reality of negative population growth and an elasticity ofsubstitution below one.

title: Housing Inequality in Spain
affiliations: Vanderbilt University - College of Arts and Science - Department of Economics and Université Libre de Bruxelles (ULB)

detail.title: Housing Inequality in Spain

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors declare no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: Gerard Domènech-Arumí gratefully acknowledges funding from Fondation ULB.

detail.abstract: We use data on the universe of real estate stock in Spain and recent transactions in Catalonia to construct novel contemporaneous and long-run estimates of housing inequality across all existing subnational levels. Housing inequality in Spain lies between Belgium and the United States, with the top 1% of the most spacious and valuable dwellings accounting for over 6% of total residential space and value. Long-run series show that space inequality was much higher at the start of the 20th century and declined markedly in the 1960s, coinciding with a housing supply boom. Housing value inequality increased between 2009 and 2019, likely due to cyclical shifts in aggregate demand and stagnation in new housing supply. We document significant heterogeneity across all levels of aggregation and a correlation between housing value and income inequality, suggesting a link between the two. This research introduces a publicly available database for studying housing-related topics and highlights the importance of granularity when evaluating inequality and housing policies.

title: UN Tax Committee Confronts New Challenges from AI to Health Taxes
affiliations: Texas A&M University (TAMU), School of Law and Texas A&M University (TAMU), School of Law

detail.title: UN Tax Committee Confronts New Challenges from AI to Health Taxes
detail.abstract: With this article, we provide our readers an overview of the United Nations’ International Tax Committee of Experts[3] most important past initiatives and those discussed and voted upon October 21 through 24, 2025, to be addressed within work streams during the four-year term that began July 30, 2025 with the announcement of the newly appointed country-delegates (who speak in their personal capacity rather than on behalf of their government positions).

title: Digital Asset Tokenization and Decentralized Finance: Reshaping Monetary Systems and Financial Infrastructure of Today
affiliations: Cracow University of Economics

detail.title: Digital Asset Tokenization and Decentralized Finance: Reshaping Monetary Systems and Financial Infrastructure of Today
detail.abstract: The convergence of real-world asset tokenization and decentralized finance protocols represents a paradigm shift in global financial architecture, challenging traditional concepts of monetary policy, financial intermediation, and economic coordination. This research proposal examines how blockchain-based tokenization of physical and financial assets, combined with programmable smart contracts and decentralized protocols, is fundamentally altering the mechanisms through which value is stored, transferred, and governed in modern economies. The study employs a mixedmethods approach combining quantitative analysis of tokenized asset markets with qualitative examination of regulatory frameworks and stakeholder perspectives across major financial jurisdictions. Our investigation addresses four critical research questions: how tokenization alters traditional concepts of ownership and liquidity; the systemic implications of DeFi adoption for monetary policy transmission; the regulatory evolution required to address risks while maintaining financial stability; and the long-term implications for global monetary coordination. The research contributes to emerging literature at the intersection of monetary economics, financial technology, and regulatory policy by providing the first comprehensive analysis of how tokenized assets and DeFi protocols interact to create new forms of financial infrastructure. Expected findings suggest that widespread adoption of asset tokenization and DeFi protocols will necessitate fundamental reconsideration of central bank capabilities, regulatory frameworks, and international monetary coordination mechanisms. The study proposes a hybrid regulatory approach that balances innovation with stability through risk-based supervision, regulatory sandboxes, and enhanced international cooperation. These contributions are essential for policymakers, financial institutions, and researchers seeking to understand and navigate the transformation of global financial systems in the digital age.

title: From Crowds to Code: Algorithmic Echo Chambers and the Normalization of Coercive Suppression in Political Life
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: From Crowds to Code: Algorithmic Echo Chambers and the Normalization of Coercive Suppression in Political Life
detail.abstract: This paper examines how algorithmic recommendation systems transform the dynamics of political speech and legitimacy. Building on classic works in mass psychology and propaganda studies-Voltaire, Le Bon, Lippmann, Bernays, Hoffer, Ortega y Gasset, Ellul, and Arendt-it argues that the rise of digital echo chambers has intensified historical processes by which absurd beliefs become normalized and coercion gains social legitimacy. The analysis introduces the concept of the digital legitimization loop, a cycle in which rhetorical labels are introduced, amplified, socially normalized, reframed as protective imperatives, and legitimized as coercive actions. Empirical illustrations are drawn from social media research, polarization studies, and comparative governance literature, including recent SSRN contributions. The paper concludes that while these mechanisms are not new, algorithms accelerate and entrench them at unprecedented speed, scale, and persistence, with profound implications for democratic pluralism and governance.

title: Neural Networks and Scott Topology: From Partial Propositions to Interval Semantics
affiliations: Thalesians

detail.title: Neural Networks and Scott Topology: From Partial Propositions to Interval Semantics
detail.abstract: We develop a domain-theoretic semantics for neural networks at two levels of abstraction. First, for Boolean MLPs we place propositional calculus on the Scott domain of partial truth assignments and prove that thresholding yields a continuous map that relates the Scott topology of partial information to the clopen (Stone) topology of total models. Second, for real-valued networks we work in the interval domain for reals and show that affine and threshold (or ReLU) layers extend to Scott-continuous transformers of intervals; the induced abstract threshold map relates the Scott topology on intervals to the Euclidean/decision-topology of the concrete network. Together these results explain how neural thresholding composes with domain information order, and how logical and geometric topologies interlock under approximation.

title: AI Chernobyl and the Collapse of Civilization: Diagnosing and Rebuilding the Architecture of Trust in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Independent Researcher, South Korea

detail.title: AI Chernobyl and the Collapse of Civilization: Diagnosing and Rebuilding the Architecture of Trust in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: This paper argues that unchecked advances in artificial intelligence (AI) risk triggering an “AI Chernobyl” – a cascading collapse of core civilizational systems analogous to a technological meltdown. The core thesis is that the acceleration of AI (and related technologies like quantum computing) has exposed an existential fragility in modern civilization: our interdependent networks of trust, governance, truth-validation, life-critical infrastructure, and value systems could rapidly unravel due to AI-induced systemic shocks. Five collapse scenarios are analyzed: a Collapse of Trust (a breakdown of public trust in institutions, media, and communication due to AI-enabled deception), a Collapse of Order (disintegration of social and political order via AI-amplified instability and conflict), a Collapse of Truth (epistemic chaos from AI-generated misinformation eroding any shared reality), a Collapse of Life (existential catastrophe from misaligned or weaponized AI causing mass loss of life), and a Collapse of Value (a nihilistic erosion of human values and meaning under pervasive AI influence). Drawing on philosophical insights (Heidegger’s critique of technology, Hans Jonas’s ethics of responsibility, Arendt’s analysis of truth and power, etc.), the paper situates these scenarios in a broader framework of technology and existential risk. A scenario-based methodology is used to explore each collapse in depth, followed by a comparative discussion relating these scenarios to contemporary AI risk research (Bostrom’s superintelligence, Ord’s existential risk estimates, Russell’s alignment problem, etc.). The analysis then turns to the philosophical implications of civilizational collapse – especially the loss of meaning and truth – before finally proposing a new “social contract” for the AI era. This new social contract rests on five principles – Radical Verifiability, Distributed Sovereignty, Epistemic Integrity, Emergent Governance, and Systemic Resilience – aimed at rebuilding the architecture of trust and ensuring that advanced AI supports, rather than undermines, the foundations of civilization. The tone throughout is rigorous and conceptual, seeking to clarify the stakes of advanced AI for philosophers and social theorists and to articulate a path toward averting collapse through enlightened governance and ethical innovation.

title: Domain-Theoretic Fixed Points, Compactness, and Continuity in Neural Networks
affiliations: Thalesians

detail.title: Domain-Theoretic Fixed Points, Compactness, and Continuity in Neural Networks
detail.abstract: We apply three classical results of domain theory-the Kleene Fixed Point Theorem, the Hofmann-Mislove Theorem, and the compactness of the Lawson topology-to neural networks via the topological correspondences between their Scott abstractions and concrete Euclidean semantics. These results establish, respectively: (i) the existence and computability of canonical fixed-point semantics for monotone recurrent and residual networks; (ii) the existence of finite, compact robustness certificates for decision regions; and (iii) the attainment of margin extrema on compact priors. Together they give a rigorous domain-theoretic foundation for convergence, robustness, and optimization in neural computation.

title: Enhancing Mathematics Instruction through Quizizz: A Systematic Literature Review
affiliations: Rhodes University, South Africa, Rhodes University, South Africa and Walter Sisulu University

detail.title: Enhancing Mathematics Instruction through Quizizz: A Systematic Literature Review
detail.abstract: This systematic review paper examines the pedagogical value of utilizing Quizizz to enhance mathematics instruction within secondary education. Guided by the PRISMA 2020 framework, the review analyzed 25 peer-reviewed studies published between 2015 and 2024, sourced from ERIC, ScienceDirect, and SpringerLink. The database searches employed specific search terms, such as "Quizizz AND mathematics," "formative assessment AND Quizizz," "educational games AND mathematics classroom," and "student motivation OR Quizizz," to ensure comprehensive coverage of relevant literature. A thematic synthesis approach was utilized, involving coding, the grouping of descriptive themes, and the generation of analytical themes to analyze the findings. The review particularly focused on Quizizz's effects on student engagement, motivation, academic performance, formative feedback, and differentiated instruction, with Self-Determination Theory (SDT) serving as the guiding framework. The results indicated that Quizizz consistently promotes active participation and motivation, with multiple studies reporting higher test scores and improved attitudes toward mathematics compared to traditional instructional methods. Quizizz facilitates realtime formative assessment, provides instant feedback, and enables educators to adjust their instructional strategies accordingly. Its gamified features, including avatars, leaderboards, and self-paced learning, create an interactive environment that supports autonomy, competence, and relatedness, as articulated by SDT. Furthermore, Quizizz allows for differentiation, accommodating students with varying skill levels to engage at their individual pace. These findings underscore the tool's potential to render mathematics classrooms more inclusive and effective. The review concludes with recommendations for integrating Quizizz with other pedagogical approaches and emphasizes the necessity for further research in rural and under-resourced contexts to ensure equitable access.

title: Fiscal Consolidation and Sovereign Debt Restructurings
affiliations: International Monetary Fund (IMF) Strategy Policy and Review Department and

detail.title: Fiscal Consolidation and Sovereign Debt Restructurings
detail.abstract: Sovereigns implement fiscal consolidation, i.e., expenditure consolidation around debt crises. We compile data on fiscal expenditure consolidation around debt restructurings with private external creditors in 1975-2020. We find that expenditure consolidation precedes preemptive restructurings or prevents restructurings-"ex ante"-, while occurs upon defaults/post-default restructurings-"ex post". We build sovereign long-term debt model with endogenous choice of preemptive and post-default renegotiations and public capital accumulation. The model quantitatively shows when both public capital and debt are high, the sovereign implements ex ante fiscal expenditure consolidation which, in turn, results in preemptive restructurings or avoiding restructurings. Data support theoretical predictions.

title: Topological Obstructions in Multilayer Perceptrons: The XOR Problem and the Topology of Deep Networks
affiliations: Thalesians

detail.title: Topological Obstructions in Multilayer Perceptrons: The XOR Problem and the Topology of Deep Networks
detail.abstract: We present a topological interpretation of the well-known XOR problem in neural networks. By assigning natural topologies to both the propositional calculus of Boolean functions and the geometric decision regions of multilayer perceptrons (MLPs), we demonstrate that the failure of a single-layer perceptron to represent XOR is a homological obstruction: its decision regions are necessarily connected, whereas XOR corresponds to a disconnected clopen subset of the Stone space of Boolean formulas. Using the Mayer-Vietoris sequence and the Nerve Theorem, we generalise this observation to a broader characterisation of the topological information content of MLPs, deriving explicit bounds on Betti numbers, duality relations, and persistence stability for deep networks.

title: Innovation-Driven Contractions: A Missing Link for Asset Pricing Puzzles
affiliations: University of North Carolina (UNC) at Chapel Hill - Finance Area and Chinese University of Hong Kong

detail.title: Innovation-Driven Contractions: A Missing Link for Asset Pricing Puzzles
detail.abstract: We provide a unified resolution for prominent conditional asset-pricing puzzles through "innovation-driven contractions." Empirically, we document two stylized facts: (1) technological innovations initially cause significant labor contractions and have negligible impact on capital, and (2) puzzling disconnections-between stock returns and either investment growth or hiring surprises-intensify under stickier prices. A two-sector New-Keynesian model quantitatively ties these facts, explaining the anomalous negative correlation between stock-returns and investment-returns, the negative market reactions to favorable labor market news, and the procyclical equity yield term-structure slope. Investment-based dividend yields filtered from our model strongly predict future returns, underscoring our mechanism's empirical applicability.

title: Indian Model of Development Partnership
affiliations: Institute for International Studies at Moscow State Institute of International Relations (MGIMO University) of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Russian Federation

detail.title: Indian Model of Development Partnership
detail.abstract: This is an abstract of the report, presented at the conference “Modern Development of Global South: Problems and Perspectives”, organised on September 24 by the Institute of Scientific Information for Social Sciences (INION) of the Russian Academy of Sciences. It deals with the main features of Indian development partnership model, its differences from traditional Western approaches and current trends in development partnership in South Asia.

title: The Sanctity of Statistics: Unpacking the Illusions in Pakistan's 113th NAC Growth Estimates
affiliations: and Pakistan Institute of Development Economics

detail.title: The Sanctity of Statistics: Unpacking the Illusions in Pakistan's 113th NAC Growth Estimates
detail.abstract: The integrity and reliability of national income statistics are foundational to sound economic policymaking, fiscal planning, and international credibility. In Pakistan, the National Accounts Committee (NAC) is mandated to present GDP estimates that reflect the true state of economic activity across sectors. However, the figures presented in the 113th NAC meeting for FY 2024–25 raise methodological and empirical concerns. Despite a visible contraction in key real sectors such as important crops, large-scale manufacturing, and mining, the NAC reports a provisional GDP growth rate of 2.68% and a nominal GDP size of $411 billion, figures that appear statistically inconsistent with observed sectoral contractions. This paper reviews the NAC’s reported growth estimates and per capita income, using a mix of official data sources, sectoral performance indicators, and established macroeconomic accounting frameworks. The review questions the coherence of the reported figures by focusing on five key areas: (1) inconsistencies between agricultural contraction and reported sectoral growth, (2) implausible volatility in the electricity, gas, and water supply sector, (3) overstatement of industrial growth despite LSM and mining decline, (4) strategic use of minimal GDP revisions to preserve political narratives, and (5) questionable conversion of GDP into dollar terms and per capita income amid currency depreciation and inflation. By dissecting these elements, the paper aims to highlight the growing need for transparency, methodological clarity, and institutional independence in national income accounting in Pakistan.

title: Performance Comparison between Actively and Passively Managed Mutual Funds
affiliations: PES University

detail.title: Performance Comparison between Actively and Passively Managed Mutual Funds
detail.abstract: Through quantitative assessment of key performance metrics, including a 5-year compound annual growth rate, volatility, Sharpe ratio, and expense ratios, this study compares actively and passively managed mutual fund performance. In addition, primary survey data includes responses regarding investor investor perceptions and preferences. The study finds, although actively managed fund performance provided better returns and risk-adjusted performance, they also had higher overall costs, expense ratios, and volatility than the passively managed mutual funds. Passively managed funds had lower costs and consistent returns that mimicked the market. Finally, the study highlights the trade-offs between chasing alpha returns and cost, while suggesting an alignment with risk tolerance and investment objectives when selecting funds.

title: Climate Finance and Green Growth: The Influence of Income Level, Sectoral Heterogeneity and Industry Specification
affiliations: Ho Chi Minh University of Banking and Nottingham Trent University

detail.title: Climate Finance and Green Growth: The Influence of Income Level, Sectoral Heterogeneity and Industry Specification

keywords: Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation; Two-stage Control Function.

detail.abstract: Based on a comprehensive national-level dataset covering 140 countries from 2000 to 2024, we investigate the relationship between international climate finance and economic growth sustainability. Employing a two-stage control function method to address endogeneity, the results show that both mitigation and adaptation funds significantly enhance green growth overall. The analysis reveals substantial heterogeneity: mitigation finance is more effective in higher-income countries with better institutional quality, while adaptation finance has broader but weaker context dependent impacts. Sectoral analysis indicates that climate finance particularly reduces carbon intensity of GDP in industrial processes and power generation sectors, highlighting targeted effectiveness. The findings emphasize that climate finance achieves stronger environmental outcomes when aligned with recipients’ income levels, institutional readiness, and sector-specific characteristics. Policymakers should therefore prioritize strengthening institutional capacities and tailoring financial interventions accordingly.

title: Monetary and Fiscal Policy Interactions in the Aftermath of an Inflationary Shock
affiliations: Bank of Portugal, Banco de Portugal, Bank of Portugal and European Central Bank (ECB)

detail.title: Monetary and Fiscal Policy Interactions in the Aftermath of an Inflationary Shock

publicationDetails.journalName: ECB: Working Paper Series (Topic)

detail.abstract: This paper studies the effect of alternative monetary policy responses and the implementation of different fiscal policy measures to an inflationary shock in a monetary union, through the lens of a global DSGE model calibrated to the euro area. We find that a more aggressive monetary policy response mitigates the inflation surge, but has a detrimental impact on economic activity that imposes a stronger increase of public debt, reducing the fiscal policy space. We also find that some fiscal policy measures may alleviate the negative impact of the shock on households and firms, but do not significantly alter the inflation dynamics: a reduction of consumption taxes reduces inflation only temporarily, while an increase of transfers or of public investment slightly increase inflation initially, even if the latter may have a protracted negative impact. Overall, an appropriate mix of monetary and fiscal policies may be needed to ensure a swift return of inflation to target, while mitigating the impact on consumption. Targeting transfers to support constrained households has a mild impact on inflation, but may be a way to mitigate the impact on the most vulnerable with a less detrimental effect on public debt.

title: Redundancy or Reforms: Review of Pakistan’s 2024–25 Agency Proliferation
affiliations: and Pakistan Institute of Development Economics

detail.title: Redundancy or Reforms: Review of Pakistan’s 2024–25 Agency Proliferation
detail.abstract: In the FY 2024–25, Pakistan’s federal and provincial governments once again introduced a long list of new agencies, authorities, and administrative units. These new bodies, launched under banners like modernization, reform, or better service delivery, cover everything from intelligence and cybersecurity to housing, education, and digital governance. On paper, this may look like progress. But when we look more closely, it becomes clear that much of this expansion follows a familiar pattern: instead of improving existing institutions, the government keeps creating new ones, often with overlapping roles and unclear responsibilities. This kind of growth doesn’t necessarily mean better governance; the government already has far too many agencies doing similar work. Moreover, the government's footprint on the economy encompasses more than 67%, not merely through public enterprises but through a sprawling and duplicative administrative apparatus. Rather than fixing what’s broken, there’s a tendency to add more layers, more departments, more directorates, more “units”. This doesn’t just waste public money; it also causes confusion, slows down decision-making, and opens the door for bureaucratic red tape and internal power struggles. At a time when Pakistan needs leaner, more efficient governance, expanding the state without fixing its inner workings risks doing more harm than good.

title: Could the Popularity of BNPL Result from Consumers' Misconceptions about the Financial Product's?
affiliations: Université Paris-Saclay, Université Paris-Saclay UFR Droit-Economie-Gestion, Poznan University of Economics and Businness, Cracow Univeristy of Economics and Lviv Polytechnic National University

detail.title: Could the Popularity of BNPL Result from Consumers' Misconceptions about the Financial Product's?
detail.abstract:
The main objective of this article is to examine the factors that may influence the misidentification of the Buy Now, Pay Later (BNPL) payment system, with a particular focus on whether its popularity is due not only to user adoption incentives but also to a fundamental misinterpretation of its financial nature. In particular, the article addresses the question to what extent consumers perceive BNPL as a financial product distinct from traditional credit and how this perception shapes their financial behavior and decision-making. Although BNPL is frequently promoted as a seamless and interest-free alternative to credit cards, growing evidence indicates that many consumers fail to recognize it as a form of debt. This misconception may stem both from deliberate marketing strategies employed by BNPL providers and from cognitive biases that influence financial decision-making. The article investigates whether consumers’ limited financial literacy, along with psychological
heuristics—such as the framing effect, present bias, and mental accounting—play a role in the rapid adoption of BNPL, often without a full awareness of its potential financial implications. The research area defined in this way is particularly interesting because it is a new approach to the analysis of deferred payments. Many studies have been conducted on the BNPL market and the structure of the financial product itself, but the source of its false perception has been very rarely addressed.
Critical analysis of the literature and previous scientific research on the subject. Empirical data verifying knowledge about BNPL and its perception by consumers come from research conducted in January 2024 using the PAPI and CAWI methods on a sample of 1002 Poles and in March 2025 using the CAWI method on a sample of 343 European students and their families. The article also refers to the positions of European financial market regulators from the perspective of actions to be taken. The conducted consumer research revealed a common misconception about the nature of the product, which is BNPL. Many people, especially young people, perceive BNPL not as a financial service (consumer credit), but as an extension of the store’s commercial offer, which in its own name and on its own behalf decides to accept deferred payment for a product or service. It was also revealed that the use of BNPL facilitates the emergence of heuristics and other behavioral factors influencing the consumers’ misconception about the nature of this financial product. The presented consumer research and scientific research studies lead to an interesting conclusion, according to which the popularity of BNPL may result to a large extent from the consumers’ misconception that it is not a form of credit. This has significant consequences for the reflection on the adaptation of consumer protection regulations on the financial market and forces specific actions on the part of financial market supervisors.

title: Transparency and Whistleblowing in Public Goods Provision with Rent-Extracting Aadministrators
affiliations: University of Birmingham - Department of Economics, Leuphana University Lüneburg and

detail.title: Transparency and Whistleblowing in Public Goods Provision with Rent-Extracting Aadministrators
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how transparency and whistleblowing influence public goods provision in the presence of administrators who may engage in rent extraction. Using a repeated public trust game experiment, we find that both institutions increase voluntary contributions by approximately 40% compared to a baseline where contributors cannot distinguish between rent extraction and low contributions. However, they operate through distinct behavioural channels. Transparency reduces the roundwise decline of contributions, while the presence of a whistleblowing institution triggers an early boost in contributions. To distinguish these mechanisms, we estimate a structural panel vector autoregressive model (PVAR).
