detail.title: Windfalls as a Curse? House Demolition and Children's Educational Attainment in China *
detail.abstract: This paper examines the impact of household wealth shocks on children's educational attainment. Exploiting China's large-scale urban demolition program as an exogenous windfall shock, we identify a significant short-term negative effect. Children whose households experienced demolition before they turned 16 are approximately 10% less likely to enroll in a high school, compared with their peers from non-demolished households. Children whose households experienced demolition between the ages of 17 and 19 are 19% less likely to enter a bachelor's degree program. After ruling out alternative explanations, we identify an underexplored mechanism: changes in household member's risky behavior. Demolition compensation increases the likelihood of household members engaging in gambling and raises overall gambling expenditure, thereby indirectly deteriorating the home environment for children. The negative impact disappears in households where parents possess higher educational attainment and better financial literacy, and it arises only when compensation is delivered in cash rather than in kind. These findings highlight a novel behavior mechanism on children's educational attainment and underscore the importance of household financial capability.

detail.abstract: The credit crisis of 2007-09 opened the unique opportunities for Islamic banks to emerge globally. Malaysia was one of the countries that were least affected by the crisis. Many analysts argued the reason for this is the early growth of Islamic finance. Malaysia has implemented the concept of Islamic banking in 1983. On contrary, Pakistan materially implemented this concept in early 2000. However, parallel Islamic banking industry is functioning in both the countries along with the conventional banks. The core objective of the study is to compare profitability determinants of Islamic banks working in Malaysia and Pakistan. The data was collected from Financial Statements of 8 full-fledged Islamic banks in Malaysia and 4 full-fledged Islamic banks in Pakistan for the period (2011-2017). Pooled OLS, Fixed effect, and Random Effect Panel regression analysis have been carried out to test the hypothesis and to compare the profitability determinants of both countries. Internal factors like Liquidity, Leverage, Efficiency, Size, and Asset quality were regressed against profitability. In addition to this, GDP per capita and inflation are also considered as macroeconomic factors in this study. However, the results show that macroeconomic factors, liquidity, efficiency, and size of Islamic bank affect the profitability of Islamic banks of both regions in the same manner. While asset quality and leverage is not a good predictor of profitability of Islamic banks in Pakistan due to developing phase of Islamic banking.

title: Job Insecurity and Equilibrium Determinacy in a Rational Expectations, New Keynesian Model with Asymmetric Information- A Theoretical Analysis
affiliations: and Italian National Research Council - Institute for Studies on the Mediterranean (CNR ISMed)

detail.title: Job Insecurity and Equilibrium Determinacy in a Rational Expectations, New Keynesian Model with Asymmetric Information- A Theoretical Analysis
detail.abstract: Despite the importance of this variable in the macroeconomic context, current research on job insecurity remains mainly confined to its non-systemic dimension. The research aim of this paper is to identify the macroeconomic determinants of job insecurity in the presence of asymmetric information between public and private agents, informative shocks, and different degrees of institutional communication transparency. To accomplish this goal, a small-scale, rational expectations, New Keynesian model is proposed in which limitedly informed households and firms receive a potentially noisy informative signal about the unobservables from a fully informed government and central bank. It is found that, notwithstanding the fulfillment of the Taylor principle, if public agents transfer all the available information to the private agents without communication ambiguities, the model admits a unique, stable equilibrium path along which the "Paradox of Transparency" can emerge. Otherwise, the model's dynamics become unpredictable in terms of equilibrium existence and multiplicity, and job insecurity plays a potentially fundamental role in equilibrium determinacy. Appropriate policy recommendations are discussed.

title: The Transition that (almost) Bankrupted a Nation! From WAPDA to Unbundled System-Six Decades of Power Sector Management in Pakistan

detail.title: The Transition that (almost) Bankrupted a Nation! From WAPDA to Unbundled System-Six Decades of Power Sector Management in Pakistan
detail.abstract: The provision of electrical power is of critical importance in any country’s economic growth and development. Since independence, Pakistan has experimented with two major systems of power provision- a vertically integrated system under WAPDA since 1959 with Production, Transmission and Distribution under a single organization, and an ‘unbundled’ system with private sector participation since early 1990s that separated these three functions, managed by over two dozen public sector entities and private sector concentrated in power production. WAPDA achieved significant national milestones but its operations were hampered by various factors that were not necessarily of its own making. The persistence of these problems led to unbundling of the WAPDA led system, ushering in private sector led IPP model and a plethora of public sector entities managing it. However, except for production, not a single target/aim that was set at the time of WAPDAs unbundling has been met. Even the production aspect has come at a hefty price to the exchequer and the consumer. The liabilities of the sector have assumed such proportions that it has put the entire fiscal operations of the federal government at stake, reflecting a poorly managed, inefficient and unproductive system. The cost-benefit analysis concludes that the previous system under WAPDA was better in terms of benefits accrued. The conclusion of this research effort is that the decision to unbundle WAPDA was poorly thought out and badly executed. In the Way Forward, it is proposed that the best strategy now is to decentralize the system to provincial level, with competition, a competitive trading market and optimizing upon relative comparative advantage at the core of the new strategy.

detail.abstract: This study investigates how large corporations can achieve sustainable growth by penetrating alternative and neglected markets amid intensifying global competition and crisis volatility. Adopting a mixed-methods design grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the research integrates quantitative analysis (n = 400) with qualitative case insights from multinational firms. Findings reveal that strategic flexibility, digital maturity, and cultural intelligence form a synergistic triad that drives superior competitive performance. The interaction between flexibility and digitalization produces multiplicative benefits, while cultural intelligence mediates innovation adoption across diverse markets. Although global crises may weaken flexibility’s direct effect, they simultaneously stimulate adaptive innovation and organizational learning. The study proposes the Integrated Framework for Alternative Market Penetration (IFAMP), a practical model linking dynamic capabilities to real-world strategy. Managerial and policy implications emphasize rapid resource reallocation, AI-enabled decision systems, and deep cultural localization. The research contributes to the advancement of dynamic capability theory, extends behavioral economics to market strategy, and reframes crises as opportunities for renewal.

title: Analyzing the Legitimacy of ESG Principles on Financial Performance Through Linear Regression Models

detail.title: Analyzing the Legitimacy of ESG Principles on Financial Performance Through Linear Regression Models
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the legitimacy of ESG (Environmental, Social, Governance) principles as predictors of stock valuation, specifically through the P/E (Price to Earnings) ratio. Using financial data from the S&P 500 retrieved via the yfinance API, we conducted linear regression analysis on 425 firms. Models tested included raw, log-transformed, and sector-adjusted specifications. Our final regression shows a statistically significant, positive relationship between ESG rating and P/E ratio, suggesting ESG-conscious firms are valued at a premium. However, EPS and Debt-to-Equity showed negative relationships with P/E, and industry effects were significant. Our findings suggest ESG ratings are priced into valuations, though causality remains unclear.

title: From Aspiration Gaps to Foreign Sales: A Prospect Theory View of Family SME Internationalization
affiliations: Chung-Ang University and Incheon National University

detail.title: From Aspiration Gaps to Foreign Sales: A Prospect Theory View of Family SME Internationalization
detail.abstract: Drawing on prospect theory, this study examines how family ownership configuration—not merely level—influences internationalization contingent on performance feedback We theorize that concentrated CEO ownership internalizes prospect theory calculations within a single decision-maker, enabling rapid risk-seeking responses below aspirations. Dispersed family ownership creates collective loss aversion through multiple evaluators with heterogeneous reference points. Analyzing 170 Korean manufacturing family SMEs (2014-2019), we find CEO ownership positively predicts foreign sales intensity while dispersed family ownership constrains expansion. Consistent with prospect theory, both ownership types exhibit amplified risk-seeking below aspirations. Critically, ownership structure moderates internationalization-performance relationships asymmetrically: risk-seeking internationalization pursued from positions of financial weakness under concentrated CEO ownership yields substantially weaker performance benefits than strategic expansion undertaken from positions of strength, revealing how governance configuration shapes not only strategic choices but also their organizational consequences. Results advance behavioral strategy by demonstrating that prospect theory's predictions are governance-contingent, not universal.

title: Dissecting the Crisis-Driven Risk Spillover Nexus Between Global Energy Commodities and Chinese Sectoral Equities: A TVP-VAR Approach Across Pandemic and Geopolitical Regimes

detail.title: Dissecting the Crisis-Driven Risk Spillover Nexus Between Global Energy Commodities and Chinese Sectoral Equities: A TVP-VAR Approach Across Pandemic and Geopolitical Regimes
detail.abstract: The increasing volatility and interconnectedness of global financial and commodity markets, particularly during systemic crises, pose critical challenges for investors and policymakers seeking to manage cross-market risks. This study investigates the dynamic return connectedness between segmented global energy and precious metals commodity markets and China’s sectoral equity indices using a Time-Varying Parameter Vector Autoregressive (TVP-VAR) framework. Utilizing daily data from January 2015 to October 2024, the research captures how return spillovers evolve across systemic events such as the COVID-19 pandemic and the Russia Ukraine war. The dataset comprises eleven S&P GSCI subindices representing global energy and precious metals markets and two Wind indices reflecting China’s energy and financial equity sectors. The empirical findings reveal that energy indices, particularly the S&P GSCI Energy Index (GEN), Petroleum Index (GPT), and Crude Oil Index (GCO), act as consistent net transmitters of return spillovers. In contrast, the S&P GSCI Precious Metals Index (GPM), along with the Wind Energy and Financial Industry Indices (CENG and CFIN), serve predominantly as net receivers. The Total Connectedness Index (TCI)and Net Pairwise Directional Connectedness (NPDC)measure show sharp intensification during major crises, highlighting the time-sensitive and asymmetric nature of global return interdependencies. Pairwise Connectedness Index (PCI) and network diagram analyses further confirm the structural shifts in spillover pathways during crisis periods. These findings offer valuable implications for market regulators, policymakers, and institutional investors by identifying dominant shock propagators and systemic absorbers. The study provides fresh empirical insights into global financial contagion mechanisms and contributes to dynamic risk monitoring and macroprudential policy design.Keywords: Connectedness; TVP-VAR; Global Commodities; Chinese Industry Stocks; COVID-19; Geopolitical Risk; Financial Contagion;JEL classification: C32; F65; G15; G18; Q43

title: The Distributional Effects of Renewable Energy, a Plant-level Analysis
affiliations: and Colorado School of Mines - Division of Economics and Business

detail.title: The Distributional Effects of Renewable Energy, a Plant-level Analysis
detail.abstract: In recent years, fossil fuel power plants have increasingly adjusted their operations to balance variability in renewable output. These balancing activities alter plant emissions in ways that may not be evenly distributed. We capture the distribution of the effect of exogenous wind and solar variation on emissions from criteria pollutants across fossil fuel plants. Most plants experience a small reduction in emissions in response to variation in renewable output. However, a minority of outlier plants change their emissions output significantly, with responses that may be either positive or negative. Positive emissions responses are driven by increases in fuel intensity or emissions rates for some plants, particularly in response to solar variation. We find that outlier plants are more likely to be in smaller Balancing Authorities, without access to electricity markets, and with higher shares of wind and solar output. The socioeconomic characteristics of communities hosting outlier power plants depend on whether the plant is wind-or solar-responsive. Notably, communities with higher asthma incidence, which are more sensitive to pollution, experience the most extreme negative emissions responses to wind, but the most extreme positive emissions responses to solar.

title: Agentic Economics: A Novel Macroeconomic Theory, Production Architecture and Dynamics of AI
affiliations: Global Blockchain Business Council

detail.title: Agentic Economics: A Novel Macroeconomic Theory, Production Architecture and Dynamics of AI
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel macroeconomic framework in which artificial intelligence (AI) serves as a distinct factor in production with its own unique role, not reducible to labor or capital. We formalize an economy-wide production architecture comprised of modular tasks and autonomous AI-driven ('agentic') processes, departing from classical Cobb-Douglas or CES formulations. The model incorporates new theoretical constructs-including modular function spaces, a control gradient of AI integration, task entropy as a measure of task complexity, and capacity thresholds in AI capability-to capture the ways AI transforms production. In this dynamic framework, AI systems optimize, repurpose and re-engineer task execution and coordination, creating new surplus channels of output. We derive testable predictions about long-run growth rates, transitional productivity dynamics, the evolution of income shares, and the need for new institutional designs. The theory predicts that AI can fundamentally alter growth regimes and income distribution: growth may accelerate nonlinearly as AI crosses key capability thresholds, while labor's income share declines absent institutional intervention. We conclude that realizing the benefits of this growth will require adaptive policies and economic institutions tailored to this novel production paradigm.

Thus, there is significant value in being able to identify “at risk” banks in a timely and accurate way. title: Crony Capitalism, Populism, and Democracy
affiliations: George Mason University and George Mason University - Department of Economics, Mercatus Center at George Mason University

detail.title: Crony Capitalism, Populism, and Democracy
detail.abstract: In the wake of the Cold War, liberal democracy was heralded by Francis Fukuyama as the "end of history", the only viable form of human governance. Three decades later, that triumphalism has faded. Liberal democratic capitalism now faces mounting criticism, particularly for enabling cronyism. In response to this, Munger and Villarreal-Diaz pose one of the most important questions in contemporary political economy: "Does capitalism in a democracy always devolve into corporatist cronyism?" They answer in the affirmative. This paper revisits their question and offers a more precise thesis: it is not democracy per se but its current institutional form that fosters cronyism. Democracy is a normative commitment to viewing one another as dignified equals, but how that commitment is realized is a matter of continual debate and institutional design. We further argue that the democratic system itself generates a backlash against cronyism in the form of populist movements. However, while these movements claim to restore power to the people and dismantle elite privilege, under existing institutional constraints, they reproduce the very pathologies they oppose. Current democratic institutions, then, suffer from a double failure: they breed cronyism, and the populist response they provoke deepens it. In short, in the current institutional setting, there is no endogenous path out of cronyism. Does this mean democracy is inherently incompatible with capitalism? We argue that it is not. The problem lies in how democracy is institutionalized. Drawing mainly on the works of James Buchanan, F.A. Hayek, Vincent Ostrom, and Don Lavoie, we outline an alternative vision for democracy.

title: Liquidity Shocks, Homeownership, and Income Inequality: Impact of Early Pension Withdrawals and Reduced Deposit

detail.title: Liquidity Shocks, Homeownership, and Income Inequality: Impact of Early Pension Withdrawals and Reduced Deposit
detail.abstract: The paper analyzes two policies that affect housing demand, one that allows early withdrawal from pension savings (EW) and one that reduces the load deposit amount (RD), in both an equal-affordability market and a supply-constrained market. A custom model that incorporates demand effects on housing prices using Australian data shows that these policies are at best ineffective or at worst harmful for housing affordability. Both RD and EW raise prices in the short run. RD tends to delay or prevent access for lower-income households, particularly in supply-constrained markets where it significantly increases inequality by relaxing constraints for higher-income households. EW modestly brings purchase timing forward across groups with limited downside for inequality. Equal-affordability and supply-constrained settings generate opposite shifts in low-income purchase timing, indicating that unequal outcomes stem not from the price surge itself but from pre-existing market disparities. Restricting the accessibility of the policies to specific income groups only marginally improves their effectiveness

title: Corporate decisions and national happiness during negative tail events – international evidence
affiliations: University of Tasmania - Tasmanian School of Business & Economics, University of Tasmania, University of Newcastle and Tasmanian School of Business and Economics

detail.title: Corporate decisions and national happiness during negative tail events – international evidence
detail.abstract: Pandemics (including but not limited to COVID-19) and global financial crises are rare events that nonetheless have far-reaching global consequences for societal mood, corporate outcomes, corporate behaviour, and individual decision-making. This study examines how national happiness influences corporate financial decisions during extreme adverse shocks. We employ an international dataset of firms from 52 countries, covering the period 2005 to 2020. We find that higher national happiness is consistently associated with stronger preference for debt financing during rare economic shocks, while the effects on investment and dividend policies are less conclusive. Our results are robust to quasi-natural experiments, an instrumental variable estimation, alternative samples, and high-dimensional fixed effects. This paper contributes to the growing behavioural finance literature by providing empirical evidence on the role of happiness in shaping corporate decisions during rare economic shocks.

title: The Field-Shi of Time: Reading History as Civilizational Retuning

detail.title: The Field-Shi of Time: Reading History as Civilizational Retuning
detail.abstract: Based on the theory of civilization system and the method of Philosophical Engineering, "Reading History" redefines the function of "history": history is not the memory of the past, but the Learning System of Civilization. This book proposes a modern interpretation of "Reading History to Repair Politics"-politics is the self-correction algorithm of civilization, and reading history is the retraining process of this algorithm. By treating historical materials as the "Training Corpus of Civilization", the author constructs a multi-layered learning framework from cognition, institution, energy to rhythm, explaining how entropy increase, institutional feedback lag, and trust collapse in historical events become physical signals of political Rhythmic Tuning failure. On this basis, this paper introduces the concept of "Rhythmic Civilization", arguing that the next stage of human civilization is not about acceleration or control, but about restoring "breath"-that is, maintaining a sustainable rhythmic balance in multiple Tension fields. Through the five-step method of Philosophical Engineering (Selection-Diagnosis-Abstraction-Mapping-Simulation), "Reading History" demonstrates a cross-disciplinary civilization self-renewal mechanism: with history as the data layer, politics as the feedback layer, and philosophy as the compilation layer, civilization can maintain self-renewal in continuous entropy increase. Starting from the mirror of history, through the analysis of political Rhythmic Tuning and system algorithms, the full text finally returns to the breathing metaphor of civilization, proposing a unified proposition that runs through history, political science, and the philosophy of AI: when reading history becomes a Rhythmic Tuning behavior, civilization truly learns to breathe.

title: Elite-Guided Adaptive Hybrid Dandelion Algorithm and Its Application in Large-Scale UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing System
affiliations: Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Guangzhou University, Royal Melbourne Institute of Technology (RMIT University), Nantong University and Minia University

detail.title: Elite-Guided Adaptive Hybrid Dandelion Algorithm and Its Application in Large-Scale UAV-Assisted Mobile Edge Computing System
detail.abstract: In large-scale Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) systems with UAV assistance, Optimizing UAV deployment, job scheduling, and resource allocation is very important in emergency rescue and catastrophe management. These systems are often deployed in highly dynamic and unpredictable environments, where communication reliability, real-time task processing, and rapid decision-making are critical. This study introduces an Adaptive Hybrid Dandelion Differential Evolution Algorithm (AH-DDEA) to address these challenges, focusing on communication coverage, energy consumption, and task delay. The proposed method determines the optimal number of UAVs using a fitness-based elimination algorithm and continuously optimizes UAV deployment through the Dandelion and Differential Evolution Hybrid Optimization Operator (DO-DE), which incorporates elite strategy and historical data feedback for the purpose of reducing the overall energy consumption of the system and the mission latency. Once optimal deployment is achieved, an iterative greedy algorithm generates the best task offloading and resource allocation strategy. Experimental results demonstrate that AH-DDEA significantly outperforms traditional and advanced algorithms in reducing energy consumption, shortening task execution delays, and minimizing the number of deployed UAVs. This research provides new insights into UAV applications in complex environments, enhancing efficiency in disaster management and emergency rescue.

title: The Growing Significance of Cryptocurrency Acceptance Research: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Growing Significance of Cryptocurrency Acceptance Research: A Systematic Review and Bibliometric Analysis
detail.abstract: The adoption of cryptocurrencies has accelerated rapidly over the past decade—particularly in recent years—yet consumer acceptance remains one of the least explored and understood dimensions in the field. This study conducts a comprehensive bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review to assess the development of consumer-focused cryptocurrency research up to 2024. Drawing from 152 peer-reviewed articles and conference proceedings indexed in Scopus and Web of Science, the paper identifies dominant research trends, methodological patterns, and theoretical frameworks. Findings indicate a rise in publication activity beginning in 2019, with a marked peak in 2023, signaling the emergence of cryptocurrency acceptance as a standalone research field. Despite this growth, the review uncovers substantial gaps in regional coverage, conceptual diversity, and empirical focus, underlining the need for targeted future research. There is a clear shift from Bitcoin-centric research to broader cryptocurrency applications, including alternative coins, hypothetical systems, and practical use cases like tourism or payment solutions. In addition to mapping thematic trends, the study synthesizes methodological practices related to sampling strategies, data collection techniques, analytical tools, and software use, offering a holistic overview of how this topic is researched. By synthesizing these insights, the study offers strategic implications primarily for researchers, by outlining concrete directions for future investigations and suggesting how the field could be shaped moving forward. At the same time, the findings also provide valuable insights for regulators and businesses aiming to better understand the broader adoption of cryptocurrency technologies.

title: PCFBL-DTC: Personalized clustered federated broad learning based on dynamic trigger condition
affiliations: Capital Normal University, Capital Normal University and Jiangxi Agricultural University

detail.title: PCFBL-DTC: Personalized clustered federated broad learning based on dynamic trigger condition
detail.abstract: Traditional federated learning (FL) methods face various challenges, including unreliable clients, huge communication consumption, and heterogeneity of data across clients. To address these challenges, we propose a new algorithm which is personalized clustered federated broad learning based on dynamic trigger condition, i.e. PCFBL-DTC. In PCFBL-DTC, to address the issue of unreliable clients and improve communication efficiency, we set dynamic trigger conditions on the client and edge server respectively and correlate the trigger condition with the prediction accuracy of the model. The model uploaded only when this condition is met, which can reduce communication costs and enhancing the robustness of the algorithm. To address the issue of data heterogeneity inherent in FL, we include edge servers into algorithm and introduce a personalized clustering mechanism. This mechanism clusters clients based on the similarity of their local data, and trains a personalized model for each cluster. At the same time, the aggregation in edge servers can mitigate communication overhead, as it alleviates the need for all clients to directly communicate with the server. Finally, experimental results demonstrate that our algorithm surpasses both FedAvg and the-state-of-the-art federated broad learning methods in terms of model accuracy, communication efficiency, and training speed.

title: ChatGPT in Higher Education: Students' Perception in Relation to ChatGPT's Usage

detail.title: ChatGPT in Higher Education: Students' Perception in Relation to ChatGPT's Usage

detail.abstract: ChatGPT, an AI-powered conversational chatbot, has been a breakthrough in the field of natural language processing. The conversational chatbot can generate text human-like responses based on text input. Consequently, students began using this application for class assignments, especially for writing creative essays. Students' growing reliance on ChatGPT made educationists concerned about its implications on education and learning. Prompted by the desire, this paper studied students' use of ChatGPT in their learning, their perceived understanding of ChatGPT's usefulness, and their perception of institutional instruction on the use of ChatGPT. Likert-scale survey questions were designed for this quantitative research study. An SPSS correlation test suggests that there is a positive correlation between the students' use of ChatGPT and their perceived understanding of the usefulness of ChatGPT. However, another correlation test suggests that there was no relationship between the level of institutional instruction students receive and their use of ChatGPT. This means that the use of ChatGPT should be monitored and controlled in a way that it cannot deter students' critical thinking ability. And that should be done from the institutional end as is done in the case of prevention and detection of academic plagiarism.

title: Engineering Victory: Translating Sun Tzu into a Systems-Based Strategic Framework
affiliations: Nanyang Technological University (NTU)

detail.title: Engineering Victory: Translating Sun Tzu into a Systems-Based Strategic Framework
detail.abstract:
This paper takes Sun Tzu (The Art of War) as its research object and proposes a 21st-century pathway for its engineering operationalization. It first revisits Sun Tzu’s overarching framework—Shi (strategic momentum), pre-battle calculation, strategic design, and strategic preservation—arguing that its logical core anticipates an early form of game-theoretic modeling: achieving “win before fighting” through the controlled interaction of variables, relations, and iterative simulation.

The study then examines the systemic complexity of the modern strategic environment, marked by multi-field overlap, fragmented decision authority, radical transparency of information, escalating governance costs in post-conflict reconstruction, and the amplification of black-swan events. It demonstrates that intuition-driven judgment and traditional pre-battle calculation are insufficient to address the evolving dynamics of 21st-century strategy.

Building on this diagnosis, the paper advances five engineering design principles: (1) maintaining the classical grand logic; (2) remapping modern Fields; (3) enabling technological pre-battle calculation; (4) establishing human–machine collaboration; and (5) achieving critical-field penetration → triggering cascading collapse (leading to systemic advantage). Case studies—ranging from U.S. Cold War strategy and China’s Belt and Road Initiative to the U.S. post-9/11 Middle East interventions and the Russia–Ukraine conflict—illustrate the explanatory power and operational feasibility of the engineered Sun Tzu framework.

Finally, the paper proposes the Sun Tzu OS Architecture, structuring its input layer, computation layer, decision-output layer, and feedback loop into a unified strategic operating system. This architecture transforms the ancient art of warfare into a modern strategic engine for cross-domain systemic competition.

The findings affirm that the core value of The Art of War endures—not as historical wisdom but as a living computational philosophy revitalized through engineering translation. In the 21st century, true strategic victory lies not merely in force or economy, but in computational capability, human–machine symbiosis, and systemic advantage.

title: Splitting the spoils: The economics of Ransomware as a Service

detail.title: Splitting the spoils: The economics of Ransomware as a Service
detail.abstract: We show that cybercriminals have leveraged a new ransomware model known as Ransomware as a Service (RaaS) to massively scale up their revenues. Using Bitcoin blockchain data, we document systematic revenue sharing amongst cybercriminals, with families charging 15% of the ransom proceeds as fees for providing their ransomware programs and their affiliates receiving the remaining 85%. Complementary analysis of negotiation transcripts also reveals that ransomware groups cultivate professional identities and attempt to portray themselves as cybersecurity consultants rather than cybercriminals. The RaaS model has enabled families to extract large ransoms and grow exponentially, transforming ransomware into a large-scale, semi-formalized industry.

detail.abstract: The digital era is giving rise to a remarkable phenomenon: individuals empowered by artificial intelligence (AI) and digital infrastructure can now operate at scales that once required entire organisations. One-person unicorns-start-ups founded and operated by a single person that achieve valuations in excess of one billion dollars-have moved from science fiction into plausible reality thanks to generative AI, automation and global online markets. At the same time, networked micro-enterprises, as exemplified by Haier's Rendanheyi model and elaborated in the concept of networked agentic organisations, show how small, self-governing units can collectively create large, resilient ecosystems. Drawing on the author's theoretical framework of the Quiet Singularity, this paper develops the concept of individualised production-production systems centred on super-empowered individuals and their AI agents. It integrates insights from management science, entrepreneurship, sociology and cognitive science and proposes research directions for understanding how these emerging forms of work reshape economic value creation and social structures. Although one-person unicorns and networked micro-enterprises represent different organisational forms, both stem from the same underlying trend: a shift from organisation-centric to individual-centric production in which AI functions as a cognitive collaborator. The paper concludes with implications for practitioners, policymakers and researchers and invites empirical studies to validate the hypotheses presented.

detail.abstract: We present the Four Tests Standard (4TS)—a vendor-neutral, formal specification that converts AI governance from claims to proofs. 4TS defines four verifiable conditions—Stop, Ownership, Replay, Escalation—and operationalizes them through Proof-Carrying Decision (PCD) objects. Each PCD is a canonical, signed artifact that encodes custody, lineage, policy gates, and replay strategy, enabling deterministic verification at deploy, policy, and inference boundaries, with a public conformance bundle enabling independent verification. Adoption profiles span LLM tools, RAG, and MLOps. This replaces post-hoc narratives with mechanically checkable evidence of control.

title: From Regulatory to Institutional Information Assurance in Artificial Intelligence Innovation: Evidence from the California Consumer Privacy Act
affiliations: and

detail.title: From Regulatory to Institutional Information Assurance in Artificial Intelligence Innovation: Evidence from the California Consumer Privacy Act
detail.abstract: How do data protection regulations affect firms' AI innovation in information assurance? Using a difference-in-differences analysis of U.S. AI patent data and text analysis of S&P 500 firms' disclosed AI strategies, this study examines the impact of the California Consumer Privacy Act on AI innovation. We find that regulation does not suppress overall AI innovation but redirects it toward "assurance AI," technologies that embed information assurance into system architectures. The regulatory effects display a J-shaped dynamic, an initial decline followed by strong growth; and they exhibit pronounced regional disparities, with high-tech regions leading and low-tech regions lagging, widening the digital divide in data protection capabilities. Firms' discourse shifts from regulatory compliance to infrastructure investment, and inventive activity concentrates on confidentiality and integrity dimensions closely tied to the CCPA's requirements. Patent citation analysis shows that firms are increasingly developing assurance AI through original designs rather than building on prior patents, suggesting a shift toward radical innovation. These developments cluster around personal data-processing technologies foundational to generative AI. Overall, the findings illustrate how data protection laws reshape both the direction and scale of innovation, as firms reallocate innovation effort over time and across regions toward information assurance and more responsible AI architectures.

detail.title: AI-Driven Financial Analytics for Supply Chain Resilience in U.S. Manufacturing
detail.abstract: This paper investigates how AI-driven financial analytics can enhance supply chain resilience in U.S. manufacturing by integrating financial intelligence with operational decision-making. The study emphasizes measure output, including capacity utilization, productivity ratios, and output variability, as a critical factor that links production efficiency to financial stability. By leveraging machine learningbased forecasting and financial stress-testing models, the proposed framework enables manufacturers to anticipate disruptions, optimize liquidity management, and evaluate the cost-effectiveness of resilience strategies (Gao, 2024; Thomas, 2024). Empirical studies suggest that the integration of predictive analytics into supply chain finance reduces volatility, strengthens supplier relations, and minimizes recovery time after disruptions (Chen & Patel, 2023; Zheng, 2025). This research contributes to ongoing debates on manufacturing competitiveness, offering a dual lens that balances financial sustainability with operational continuity. The findings provide actionable insights for executives, policymakers, and supply chain managers seeking to align financial resilience with longterm output stability and innovation in the U.S. manufacturing sector (Deloitte, 2024; Kumar & Johnson, 2023).

detail.title: Digital Transformation in Financial Services: How Information Systems Drive Workforce Efficiency and Strategic Growth
detail.abstract: The financial services industry is undergoing a profound digital transformation fueled by advances in information systems (IS), automation, and data-driven technologies. This paper examines how the integration of modern information systems enhances workforce efficiency and supports strategic growth within financial institutions. Through a mixedmethod analytical framework combining enterprise data analytics, workflow process mapping, and case-based evaluations, the study identifies key drivers of operational efficiency, including intelligent automation, knowledge management systems, and predictive analytics. The findings reveal that organizations leveraging robust IS infrastructures achieve measurable improvements in decision speed, accuracy, and employee performance, while also fostering innovation and adaptability in dynamic market conditions. Additionally, the study highlights the role of digital leadership, organizational learning, and system interoperability in bridging the gap between technological adoption and sustainable strategic outcomes. By linking workforce productivity with enterprise-wide digital maturity, this research underscores the strategic imperative of aligning information systems investments with human capital optimization and long-term business objectives.

title: Creating Safe Digital Spaces
affiliations: Indian School of Business and National University of Singapore

detail.title: Creating Safe Digital Spaces
detail.abstract: Digital spaces created by modern day platforms have come to shape the way we connect today and live as a global community. However, with their increasing roles in our lives, it is becoming more and more evident that they also come with a new set of risks of harm. In this chapter, we look at how these harms can be mitigated to create digitally safe spaces. We argue that platforms need to make changes at the institutional design level rather than just police content. We first propose a framework to categorize digital harm, based on its nature and scope. Then, we develop a multi-layered sociotechnical model to analyze both the sources of harm and the points of intervention (at the micro, meso and macro level). This is followed by a discussion on key challenges and trade-offs that the platform leaders and policymakers face. Overall, the chapter presents a new framework for understanding how digital safety can be embedded into the very foundation of platforms-shifting the focus from reactive responses to proactive design.

title: When Machines Move Markets: The Systemic Risks of Generative AI in Financial Markets
affiliations: Australian National University (ANU), City University of Hong Kong (CityU) - Department of Information Systems, Australian National University (ANU) and Arizona State University (ASU) - Department of Information Systems

detail.title: When Machines Move Markets: The Systemic Risks of Generative AI in Financial Markets
detail.abstract: This paper examines the potential risks that generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) poses to financial market stability. While GenAI tools can improve informational signals for retail traders by reducing idiosyncratic noise, they may also synchronize errors across users due to shared, systematic vulnerabilities inherent in the system (e.g., correlated hallucination-induced errors across users). We develop a theoretical model in which retail investors rely either on dispersed legacy signals (the benchmark case) or on a popular LLM that may be subject to shared vulnerabilities, manifesting as correlated errors or shared biases arising from common data, model architecture, or algorithmic flaws (e.g., hallucinations). GenAI adoption thus transforms independent idiosyncratic errors into shared systematic biases that amplify volatility, distort asset prices, and reduce social welfare, particularly when the variance of the shared bias is large. The risks are further exacerbated when malicious actors exploit GenAI systems through prompt injection or data poisoning, profitably steering retail demand away from fundamentals. Moreover, once retail traders recognize the presence of shared vulnerabilities, coordination failures can arise, triggering self-fulfilling crashes even in the absence of fundamental shocks. Our analysis also highlights the stabilizing role of informed institutional investors, whose accuracy and market share determine the extent to which retail distortions are transmitted to prices. From a policy perspective, the findings highlight the importance of strengthening GenAI robustness, enhancing monitoring to detect correlated vulnerability or biases, and reinforcing the role of informed traders in counteracting biased retail demand.

detail.title: Design and Deployment of a Data-Driven Financial Analysis Model Using Predictive Analytics and ERP Integration
detail.abstract: The increasing need for real-time financial intelligence in complex organizational environments has accelerated the adoption of predictive analytics and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) integration. This study presents the design and deployment of a data-driven financial analysis model that combines predictive algorithms with ERP-based financial data to enhance decision-making accuracy and operational efficiency in manufacturing and service enterprises. The model employs advanced machine learning techniques, specifically regressionbased prediction and anomaly detection, to forecast liquidity, profitability, and cash flow trends while reducing manual processing time by 40%. Data was collected from ERP systems and financial databases of selected organizations and processed using Python-based predictive modules. The integration architecture ensures continuous synchronization between transactional ERP data and predictive dashboards, enabling proactive financial management and scenario analysis (Kumar & Sharma, 2024; Davis et al., 2023). The study findings indicate that predictive analytics, when embedded within ERP frameworks, significantly improves forecasting precision and supports realtime financial risk assessment (Anderson, Patel, & Lin, 2025). The resulting model demonstrates that organizations leveraging integrated predictive analytics outperform traditional financial systems in resilience, transparency, and scalability (Rodriguez et al., 2023; Chen & Li, 2024). This research contributes to the growing body of digital finance innovation by providing a replicable implementation pathway for intelligent financial decision-support systems.

title: AI Agents, Productivity, and Higher-Order Thinking: Early Evidence From Software Development

detail.title: AI Agents, Productivity, and Higher-Order Thinking: Early Evidence From Software Development
detail.abstract: How are agentic AI systems affecting productivity and the cognitive experience of work? This paper studies the effects of agents on software development by analyzing the impacts of an AI-assisted programming platform. In 2024, the platform released a coding agent that allows its users to generate code from natural language instructions. While the majority of users work in software roles, there is also a cohort of frequent agent users across non-engineering roles like design and product management. More experienced workers are more likely to accept agent-generated code—one standard deviation higher work experience corresponds to 6% higher accept rates. This positive experience gradient for agent accepts contrasts with a negative experience gradient for AI autocompletion accepts, as well as a junior worker skew among other kinds of AI tools. A difference-in-differences analysis of weekly code merges indicates that software output increased by 39% after the agent became the platform’s default code generation mode. Agents may shift the production process from the syntactic activity of typing code to the semantic activity of instructing and evaluating agents. User messages to agents include instructions to implement, explain, and plan. Experienced workers are more likely to develop plans in their initial messages to agents, which could improve alignment with user intent. These results suggest that abstraction, clarity, and evaluation may be important skills for workers.

title: Will Rare Earth Rivalries Reshape Web3 Amid U.S.-China Tensions?

detail.title: Will Rare Earth Rivalries Reshape Web3 Amid U.S.-China Tensions?
detail.abstract: This paper explores the potential ramifications of escalating geopolitical conflicts between the United States (and its Western allies) and China concerning rare earth elements (REEs) and metals on the Web3 ecosystem. REEs are critical for hardware underpinning blockchain technologies, cryptocurrency mining, and decentralized applications. China's near-monopoly on REE production (over 90% of global refined output) positions it as a pivotal player in global supply chains. Amid recent trade tensions, including China's export restrictions and U.S. tariffs as of October 2025, disruptions could lead to hardware shortages, increased mining costs, market volatility in cryptocurrencies, and shifts toward decentralized supply chain solutions using blockchain. The framework analyzes historical context, direct impacts, economic ripple effects, and mitigation strategies, drawing on current geopolitical dynamics. Ultimately, such conflicts may accelerate Web3 innovations in supply chain transparency and resource tokenization while posing risks to global decentralization efforts.

detail.abstract: This research examines the intricate relationship between cross-border trade liberalization, digital business transformation, and economic development in emerging markets. Through a mixed-methods approach combining quantitative trade flow analysis and qualitative case studies from BRICS nations and Southeast Asian economies, this study identifies three critical mechanisms through which international commerce catalyzes organizational change: technological adoption pressures, competitive restructuring imperatives, and institutional modernization requirements. The findings reveal that emerging market enterprises engaging in cross-border trade demonstrate 43% higher rates of digital transformation adoption compared to domestically-focused counterparts, while simultaneously facing asymmetric regulatory burdens that create a 2.7-year implementation lag relative to developed market competitors. This research contributes to international business literature by proposing an integrated framework linking trade exposure intensity with transformation velocity, mediated by institutional quality and technological infrastructure. Policy implications suggest targeted intervention strategies for emerging economies seeking to maximize transformation benefits while mitigating displacement costs associated with rapid internationalization.

detail.abstract: This article presents a case study in the design, implementation, and evaluation of a generative AI-powered simulated client used in a university-level constitutional law course. Developed entirely by a legal academic without prior programming experience, the project demonstrates how emerging "no-code" AI tools can enable educators to build complex, interactive learning environments at minimal cost. The simulated clientan AI voice agent named Alex Wong-was created using ElevenLabs and OpenAI systems to allow students to conduct live, voice-based client interviews within a web interface. The exercise operationalized principles of experiential learning, authentic assessment, and reflective practice, situating abstract constitutional concepts within a realistic legal problem that students had to investigate and analyze. Using a mixedmethods approach combining thematic analysis of interview transcripts, post-exercise surveys, and instructor observations, the study explores the simulation's pedagogical effectiveness and identifies key design challenges, including the mitigation of AI "hallucination" risks and the maintenance of factual consistency. Findings suggest that the simulation successfully promoted active engagement, deeper conceptual understanding, and self-reflection among students while remaining accessible and replicable for non-technical educators. By documenting both process and outcome, the article contributes to the emerging discourse on AI as a creative pedagogical partner and offers a transparent model for integrating generative AI into experiential legal education.
